ideas.title: Fixed-threshold, history-crossed re-read: benign-processing false-alarm rate and worst-pool miss rate
ideas.mechanism: Fix one threshold per detector on development genuine photos (false-alarm rate 5% and 10%) and never refit it per cell. Report (1) the false-alarm rate on the same test photos after each benign variant that already exists and is already scored (E7 shrink-and-enlarge, JPEG 90 / 70 / 50, blur1, resample50) and on other photo sources (FEI, FFHQ); (2) the miss rate per morph family at the threshold that keeps every gated genuine pool at or below the target (worst-pool MACER); (3) the crossed table morph variant by genuine variant, whose conflict cells (genuine more processed than the morph) and laundering cells (morph processed, genuine native) show both failure directions. Per-cell D-EER hides all three because it refits the threshold in every cell.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: A detector that follows processing history cannot satisfy both numbers at once: either the threshold moves up to protect processed genuine photos and morphs are missed, or genuine photos are flagged. Both sides are varied (genuine and morph), so the objection that E7 only damages the genuine side does not apply. No image is made; every variant exists.
ideas.covers: Landmark: full crossing on the four FRLL-Morphs tools. GAN: full crossing on FRLL StyleGAN only (MIPGAN needs variants of the corrected MAD22, which do not exist). Diffusion: genuine side only (E7 pools of MorDIFF and six DiM families; no morph-side variants). It cannot separate blend from second identity.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: CPU re-read of existing score files. Rows: /home/narolski/mambamorph-code/smadcvpr_data/manifests/eval.csv (44,666 rows; sets frllm, mordiff, dim; variants orig, resmatch, jpeg90, jpeg70, jpeg50, blur1, resample50; devbona 5,033 genuine development images; exclude set mad22 (old subset) and variant chip). Scores: /home/narolski/mambamorph-code/smadcvpr_runs/A12_scored/A12REL/<10 release variants>/scores_eval.npz (all 44,666 rows present, checked for three releases), SelfMAD own crop from experiments/A32-RSX_resolution-shortcut/raw/selfmad_own_eval.npz, and A12BR M3 (8 seeds) and M3L (5 seeds) scores_eval_last.npz. Source axis: scores_gtest.npz (FEI photos) and scores_ffhqm.npz (FFHQ photos). Decisive number: false-alarm rate of the ViT-L/14 release and of M3L on E7 and JPEG 70 photos at the native 5% threshold, per landmark family, and their miss rate at the worst-pool threshold.
ideas.falsifier: The metric is dropped if, over the 10 release variants plus M3 and M3L, the ranking by worst-pool miss rate agrees with the ranking by native D-EER at Kendall tau 0.8 or more and no network's family-mean miss rate rises by 20 points or more when the threshold moves from native to worst-pool. For our own detector: not shortcut-free if the false-alarm rate exceeds 10% on any gated pool at the native 5% threshold.
ideas.compute: CPU only, 1 to 2 hours including a one-page registration (PROTOCOL rule: only a separately registered read may use the E5 variant rows). Zero GPU. Later: about 1 GPU-hour to repeat the release rows through their own crops.
ideas.main_risk: A12REL scores are on our 512-pixel frames, not the releases' own crops (reproduction gate: ViT-B/16 MorDIFF 4.9 here against 1.10 published), so the table must be labelled and later repeated on the own-crop path. FRLL has 204 photos, so 5% is 10 images and intervals are wide. A reviewer may call JPEG 50 unrealistic, so only E7, JPEG 90, JPEG 70 and resample50 are gated. The E5 variants are outside the list of explicitly approved paths in the current brief and need the author's yes.
ideas.closest_prior_work: NIST FATE MORPH reports false detection separately for mugshot, visa and source pools at fixed operating points; top Greedy-DiM systems show visa false detection 0.29 and 0.93 (local note on the Sept 2026 report; NIST page found by search, checked; report PDF not opened by me). Peng et al., arXiv:2611.00074: a threshold set on one dataset's genuine data does not transfer to the other (checked, abstract page). Ribeiro et al., CheckList, ACL 2020 (checked that the paper exists; the invariance-test naming is from memory). In the record: A36 H-new-87 (ViT-L/14 release 5.4 / 5.9 / 13.2 / 52.9 % false alarms for original / JPEG 90 / 70 / 50).

ideas.title: Null rows first: morph-blind leaderboard, null-conditional skill, and a repaired file list (FRLL-C)
ideas.mechanism: For each benchmark cell, score models that cannot know what a morph is: file attributes, six colour statistics, border mask, expression label, 32-pixel thumbnail, an untrained network and the morph-free network (AD4). Print them as the top rows of the native table. For each detector report its paired excess over the best null, and its AUC within quintiles of the best null's score (overlap-weighted); where the classes do not overlap in the null score, the cell is marked as unable to measure morph detection. Publish the repaired file lists (expression-balanced, overlap-weighted, E7-matched) so other labs can re-read their own scores without our images.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Skill is credited only where it exceeds what a morph-blind model reaches on the same images, so every cue a null can read is subtracted, including cues nobody named (the morph-free network finds them itself). State-of-the-art comparisons are then restricted to cells that can measure the task.
ideas.covers: Landmark, GAN and diffusion at the benchmark level. It does not show what a detector reads inside a diagnostic cell, and it misses cues that no null contains (the renderer cue on MIPGAN cells until a render-against-camera null exists).
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Step 1 (existing scores only): for the 11 expression-unbalanced cells found in /home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/C_cue_checks/result.md (six DiM, five FRLL-Morphs), recompute each release's EER with the genuine class restricted to the 102 neutral photos (ids NNN_03) and then to the 102 smiling photos, from A12REL scores_eval.npz. Step 2: null rows from c_checks.json (colour regression 0.71 to 1.00 on aligned crops), the A41 file table, E07 border fractions (0.99 to 1.00) and the A47 I-3 morph-free scores (3 seeds; AD4 with 5 seeds when it lands). Count the cells whose best non-content null stays below AUC 0.90.
ideas.falsifier: Dropped if 10 or more of the 17 cells are diagnostic, or if on every cell with overlap each release's null-conditional AUC is within 0.03 of its raw AUC. The expression row of the cue table is crossed out if neutral-only and smiling-only genuine pools give EERs within 2 points for every release. Prediction from the record: the morph-free M3 network already reaches 0.0 to 2.6% EER on 11 to 12 of 17 cells, so at most 5 or 6 cells can be diagnostic.
ideas.compute: CPU minutes to 1 hour. AD4 (about 21 H100-hours) is already registered and queued.
ideas.main_risk: A reviewer can say a null is too strong: a thumbnail may legitimately carry average-face information. So admissibility is decided on non-content nulls and the morph-free network only, and content nulls are printed separately. The morph-free result was checkpoint-sensitive in A47 (0.00% at the last checkpoint, 14.5 to 20.4% at the early one), and its label-permuted control failed, so the paper needs AD4's five seeds and its reference networks before this table is final.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Poliak et al., Hypothesis Only Baselines in Natural Language Inference, *SEM 2018, arXiv:1805.01042 (checked). Gururangan et al. 2018, annotation artifacts (memory). Grommelt et al., Fake or JPEG, arXiv:2403.17608 (checked: removing JPEG and size bias changes cross-generator results by more than 11 points). Overlap weighting, Li, Morgan and Zaslavsky 2018 (memory). No such table for morph detection was found by the literature note 03; I did not repeat that search.

ideas.title: Leaderboard rank predicted from genuine photos alone: a population audit over about 295 networks and a morph-free exposure score
ideas.mechanism: For every already-scored network compute statistics that use genuine images only: mean logit shift of the FRLL photos under E7, JPEG 70, blur1 and resample50; AUC of one-identity StyleGAN3 renders against FRLL photos; score spread on the development genuine pool. Predict each network's native EER per benchmark cell from these numbers, leaving one recipe out at a time. If the diffusion and GAN leaderboards can be predicted without scoring a single morph, while a clean landmark skill measure (H1) predicts them no better, the leaderboard order is an order of reactions to processing. The fitted predictor is then an exposure score any lab can compute for a new detector from genuine photos.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: It uses no morph and no control image built by us, so it cannot be blamed on artefacts of our twins or on how realistic E7 is. It is a third, independent line of evidence beside the intervention on data (E7) and the intervention on training (morph-free network).
ideas.covers: Benchmark-level statement for diffusion and GAN cells (expected strong) and for landmark cells (expected weak, which is the informative contrast). It says nothing about identity reading and nothing about a single detector's mechanism.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: 285 runs in /home/narolski/mambamorph-code/smadcvpr_runs/A12_scored/A12BR (scores_eval_es.npz and scores_eval_last.npz) plus the 10 release variants in A12REL; rows from eval.csv (frllm, mordiff, dim; genuine variants orig, resmatch, jpeg70, blur1, resample50); render rows from scores_h3sg3.npz; skill reference from scores_h1poisson.npz (releases; the A36 raw results for retrains). Number: leave-one-recipe-out Spearman correlation between predicted and observed native EER on the seven diffusion cells, with a bootstrap over recipes.
ideas.falsifier: Dead if the leave-one-recipe-out Spearman correlation is below 0.5 on the seven diffusion cells, or if H1 skill alone predicts within 0.1 of the genuine-only predictors.
ideas.compute: CPU, about 30 minutes. Zero GPU.
ideas.main_risk: Only about nine recipe families, so few independent clusters; the early and last checkpoint of one run are not independent; releases were scored on our frames; some arms were trained with our own data and must be labelled. It is correlational and must sit beside E7 and AD4, never alone. Only arms listed in the A36 network table and used in A41 or AG5 should be read, so that no sealed arm is touched.
ideas.closest_prior_work: In the record: A36 amendment 1 (morph-against-camera AUC tracks render-against-camera AUC, Spearman 0.95 over 38 rows) and A19 (0.75 with native width). D'Amour et al., Underspecification, arXiv:2011.03395 (checked). Miller et al. 2021, accuracy on the line (memory).

ideas.title: Two-dose specificity test: morph dose must move the score, benign dose must not
ideas.mechanism: Two ladders per detector on the same hosts: a morph-dose ladder (mixing 0, 0.1 to 0.5, same tool, same pair, same storage) and a benign-dose ladder (shrink factor 1.0 to 3.3; JPEG 90 and 70). Three numbers: the Page trend p-value on the morph ladder; the step fraction (share of the 0 to 0.5 logit rise that happens between 0 and 0.1); the benign shift at the largest gated dose in units of the genuine-score SD, with an equivalence test at 0.25 SD. The dose specificity index is the morph-ladder rise divided by the largest benign shift. A physical reference exists: blending scales independent noise variance by alpha^2 + (1 - alpha)^2, so a blend reader shows about 36% of its rise by 0.1, while a pipeline reader shows about 100%.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Along the morph ladder the label and the pipeline are constant and only the dose changes; along the benign ladder only the processing changes. A cue reader produces a step on the first ladder and a slope on the second, and cannot produce a ramp on one and a flat line on the other.
ideas.covers: Landmark now (FaceMorpher graded set, 300 hosts by 6 levels; OpenCV has no graded path). GAN if AG3 runs (80 pairs by 4 levels). Diffusion only with new graded DiffAE mixes at 20 steps (about 1 GPU-hour on the DGX; not built). The plain morph ladder does not separate blend from identity; subtracting a same-person ladder (host with own second photo) does.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Score the AR2 graded FaceMorpher set (being built under /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1) with the four releases and M3 / M3L: minutes. Benign ladder from the A44 dose ladder on 185 genuine photos (ViT-B/16 release: plus 1.45 logits at 3.30x, Spearman 1.0; ViT-L/14 release: no reaction) and the A41 SelfMAD ladder (AUC 0.584 / 0.896 / 0.998 at 1.0x / 1.47x / 3.19x), both existing.
ideas.falsifier: A reads-morphing claim fails if the step fraction is above 0.8, or the Page p-value is above 0.01, or the benign shift is above 0.5 SD. As a contribution the test is demoted to a supplement figure if all four releases reach a specificity index above 5 on landmark morphs (then it does not discriminate).
ideas.compute: CPU build already running; under 0.5 GPU-hour of scoring.
ideas.main_risk: FaceMorpher at mixing 0 returns almost the photo (one grey level in about 14% of pixels), so the first step also switches the warp and blend on; the step fraction is therefore read against the same-person ladder. Only one landmark tool has a graded path. The per-image scores of the A44 ladder were not located by me.
ideas.closest_prior_work: In the record: A44 (benign dose ladder), plan items M6 / T6 (dose as a training target; here it is an evaluation). CheckList directional tests (memory). Geirhos et al., ICLR 2019, cue-conflict images, arXiv:1811.12231 (checked).

ideas.title: Ruling-proof three-class protocol with one network and two declared outputs
ideas.mechanism: Treat the one-identity render or reconstruction as its own declared class in every generator cell and report a three-row flag-rate table at one threshold (camera or processed photo; one-identity render; two-person morph) with two policy columns: A, the render is genuine and its flags are false alarms; B, the render is manipulated and its flags are hits. The detector is one network with two outputs trained on the ladder rungs: blend or two-identity evidence, and synthetic-render evidence. The reported decision is output 1 under policy A and the larger of the two under policy B, fixed before scoring. The paper then stays valid under either ruling and can post competitive native numbers on GAN and diffusion cells that are honestly labelled as render detection.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Output 1 never sees a class difference in rendering (its negatives include one-identity renders of the same generator) and output 2 never sees a class difference in morphing (its positives include one-identity renders), so each training contrast holds exactly one factor. The table shows which factor carries each benchmark number for every detector.
ideas.covers: GAN and diffusion (its purpose). Landmark is unaffected: output 2 should stay silent there, which is itself a check. It cannot make latent morphs detectable as morphs.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Zero compute: build the three-class table for the released detectors from /home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/AD1/ad1_ladder.json and experiments/AG5/ag5_ladder.json (already known: reconstructions flagged at 82 to 99.5% at benchmark thresholds; render against morph 0.40 to 0.49). Minutes: two linear heads on cached frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 features. Synthetic head trained on StyleGAN3 one-identity renders (/mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a37_sg3ctl, h3 genuine renders) and DiffAE reconstructions of FRGC / FERET photos (/mnt/t7/smad_research/diffae-expanded123-v1, about 400 reconstruction-role images) against their source photos; tested on generators not trained on: A43 arm D20 against FRLL photos, and H4b StyleGAN v1 host renders against CASIA crops.
ideas.falsifier: Dead as a route to native competitiveness if the synthetic head's AUC on a held-out generator is below 0.85 (frozen CLIP ViT-B/16 reference in the record: 0.92 render against camera), or if output 1 flags more than 10% of one-identity renders at its own 5% threshold.
ideas.compute: Heads: minutes on the DGX. LoRA version with five seeds: about 5 to 8 GPU-hours.
ideas.main_risk: It needs the author's ruling, or the decision to print both policies, and a ruling that a content-based synthetic-render output is not a gate on source. Reviewers may call policy B an AI-image detector and ask for AI-image baselines. Taking the larger of two outputs could be read as fusion (it is one network and one forward pass). Cross-generator transfer of render detection is the known weak point of that field.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Guillaro et al., B-Free, arXiv:2412.17671 (checked: fakes are regenerations of real images so the pair differs only in the generator trace). ISO/IEC 20059:2025 scope: sample modifications and manipulations, with a focus on those that amount to a multiple identity attack (checked through a search summary of the ISO page; normative text not read). SMDD, the field's standard training set, already labels one-identity StyleGAN2 renders as genuine (record and memory).

ideas.title: Additive paired ladder with a warp-only rung and a morph-side history swap
ideas.mechanism: (1) Replace d-prime shares by per-host paired mean-logit steps: each host's scores on R0, R1, R2, R3, R4 form a path, the step shares are mean paired differences over the mean total and sum to 1 by construction; next to it the flag rate at one threshold on every rung. (2) Add rung R2w for landmark tools: the host photo warped to the mid geometry of the host and its own second photo with texture weight 1.0 on the host (the library's own warp function, blend skipped). OpenCV's R2 is bit-identical to the photo and FaceMorpher's differs by one grey level, so today the step R0 to R2 is zero by construction and a reader of warp resampling would be labelled as reading morphing. (3) Fill the missing morph-side margin: our same-pair morphs at tool size against the published morphs, crossed with native and E7 photos; the conflict cell (our tool-size morphs against E7 photos) is the strict landmark test on FRLL persons.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Each step changes one thing on paired material: benchmark history (R0 to R1), warp resampling with no blend and no second face (R1 to R2w), blend with the person's own second photo (R2w to R3), second person (R3 to R4). A processed genuine photo is therefore tested at every kind of processing a morph tool applies.
ideas.covers: Landmark fully. GAN and diffusion: only the additive decomposition and the flag-rate ladder apply; R2w has no analogue there.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Parts 1 and 3 are re-reads: AD1 per-rung scores (ad1_ladder.json sources under /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a43/a43_out) now, and the AR1 bridge sets (1,221 OpenCV and 1,222 FaceMorpher same-pair morphs) when their scores land; CPU minutes. Part 2: the 300 AR2 hosts through the FaceMorpher library on CPU, about 1 hour, after an 8-image check that the warp output at blend weight 0 equals the mixing-0 frame of the unchanged loop for identical points; scoring takes minutes.
ideas.falsifier: R2w is dropped if its share of the R0 to R4 mean-logit rise is below 0.10 for all four releases. If its share is above 0.5 for a release, that release's landmark verdict changes from reads morphing to reads the warp. The additive shares replace d-prime shares only if they stay within minus 0.1 to 1.1 on AD1, where d-prime shares gave 1.10 to 1.24 and negative values.
ideas.compute: CPU 1 to 2 hours; under 0.5 GPU-hour.
ideas.main_risk: Mean-logit shares depend on the score scale (SelfMAD is nearly binary), so the stored no-TTA logits are used and the rank-based numbers are printed beside them. A warp to the person's own second-photo geometry is small and may under-represent the warp in a two-person morph; a warp to the second person's geometry is printed as descriptive only, since it moves shape toward another person. R2w is a modified warp path and needs the author's yes plus the verification step.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Gardner et al., contrast sets, arXiv:2004.02709 (checked). Geirhos et al., cue conflict, arXiv:1811.12231 (checked). In the record: the A43 two-by-two (published against same-pair morphs, two against one identity) and the five-rung ladder of 11_AUDIT_PLAN.md.

objections_to_current_plan: Objection 1: the main contrast (R2 against R4) is not one thing across families, and for generators it rests on a ruling that has not been made. For landmark tools R2 is the untouched photo (OpenCV bit-identical, FaceMorpher within one grey level), so the R0 to R2 share is zero by construction and any detector that reads warp resampling or blend is awarded 'reads morphing'. For generators R2 is a reconstruction that many biometrics reviewers will call a manipulated image; AD1 shows every release, including the 'robust' ViT-L/14, flags it (R0 to R2 AUC 0.88 to 0.99; R2 against R4 0.40 to 0.49). The same rule therefore tends to say 'reads morphing' on landmark and 'reads the benchmark' on generators partly by definition. What answers it: the author's ruling, or printing both policies with the three-class table (idea 5); the argument that SMDD, the field's own training set, labels one-identity renders as genuine and that ISO/IEC 20059 targets multiple identity attacks; a non-trivial landmark negative (E7 photos against published morphs, plus the warp-only rung of idea 6); verdicts on flag rates at one fixed threshold.

Objection 2: the method half is circular and has little method novelty, and its benchmark table will look bad. TwinMAD is CLIP with LoRA (the MADation recipe) trained on the constructions it is tested on, built by the same pipeline. A reviewer will say 'you defined a test your training matches' and 'give MADation your data: the gain is the data'. If generator reconstructions are training negatives, the detector will sit near chance on native MIPGAN, MorDIFF and DiM cells where competitors post 1 to 8%. What answers it: a two-by-two of recipe by data (comparator recipe on our data, our recipe on SMDD) on frozen features first; a primary endpoint declared now that is external to our build (published FRLL-Morphs against existing E7 photos; bar 1.0 / 1.0 / 14.7 / 4.4 % for the ViT-L/14 release) with a held-out tool and an unseen photo source; the null rows on top of the native table (a network that never saw a morph scores 0.0% on MorDIFF); the expected sign of our native loss stated before scoring; honest framing as protocol, audit and a data principle, with the detector deliberately simple.

Objection 3: the statistics and the comparators are fragile. The reproduction gate failed for every row in AD1 (ViT-B/16 5.4% against 1.10 published; ViT-L/14 26.0 against 19.3; SelfMAD has no published number in the record), yet verdict words are printed. Each release is one checkpoint. Verdicts hinge on AUC cut-offs of 0.75 and 0.65 and on d-prime shares that are not additive (1.10 to 1.24, and negative). With about 100 persons an AUC interval is about plus or minus 0.08, so most FRLL cells will read 'mixed'. Gate 1 (lower bound above 0.55 on twins) is far below a usable detector and is on the side study, not on the ruled main contrast. No operating point is a decision quantity. What answers it: score the ladder arms through the reproduced own-crop paths before any verdict (ViT-B/16 MorDIFF 0.99 against 1.10 there); the retrain blocks M3 and M3L (13 networks, last checkpoint) as the method-level row; additive paired steps and flag rates at fixed thresholds (ideas 1 and 6); the 536-host FRGC and colorFERET pool as primary; one primary family of tests (landmark ladder and AD4) and everything else descriptive.

Additional: scope against time. About 35 experiment IDs for three days, nothing yet scored on the corrected MAD22, the MIPGAN build for x86 not ready, and the author has twice objected to time spent on image generation. The standard benchmark table could be empty on 14 Nov. What answers it: freeze a minimal paper set tonight (the re-read of existing scores, AR1 to AR4, AD1, AD4, landmark T4 with five seeds, corrected MAD22 scoring of at most eight networks) and cut the rest (see the drop list).

Additional: the same-person morph is counted as a morph by the author, but under the ISO reading it is not an attack because no second person can use the document. A reviewer can object from either side. What answers it: keep it as a separately labelled column in every table and never inside the headline miss rate.

evaluation.sota_definition:
OPERATIONAL DEFINITION. One network (seed mean of five, last checkpoint, all five seeds printed, no selection on any test person). Thresholds come from development persons only and one threshold serves all families.

State of the art means S1 to S3 together.
S1 (primary, declared before scoring): landmark morphs against history-matched genuine photos. Set (a): published FRLL-Morphs FaceMorpher, OpenCV, AMSL and WebMorph against the existing E7 photos (204 photos, 102 persons). Bar: released MADation ViT-L/14 at 1.0 / 1.0 / 14.7 / 4.4 % EER (mean 5.3); its recipe retrain M3L, five seeds, 0.4 / 0.3 / 14.5 / 7.6 (mean 5.7); best AMSL of any analysed network 11.4 (M3 retrain). Set (b): the FRGC plus colorFERET ladder (536 hosts), two training tools plus one tool never trained on. Metric: miss rate (MACER) at the threshold that keeps the false-alarm rate (BSCER) at or below 5% and 10% on every genuine pool of the development persons (native, E7, JPEG 90, JPEG 70, pipeline-only); D-EER and AUC beside it. The claim is allowed if the paired person-bootstrap difference to the ViT-L/14 release and to the M3L seed mean has its upper bound below 0 on the family mean, and no family is worse by more than 1 point (FaceMorpher, OpenCV) or 3 points (AMSL, WebMorph). Visible target: AMSL under E7 below 10%.
S2 (benign processing): at the threshold giving 5% false alarms on native development photos, at most 10% on each gated benign pool (E7 at the existing kernels, JPEG 90, JPEG 70, resample50) and on two unseen photo sources (FEI, FFHQ). JPEG 50 and blur1 are printed, not gated. Reference: the released ViT-L/14 goes 5.4 / 5.9 / 13.2 / 52.9 % for original / JPEG 90 / 70 / 50; at benchmark thresholds the E7 photos of the MorDIFF pool are flagged at 54 / 51 / 98 % by ViT-B/16 / ViT-L/14 / SelfMAD.
S3 (native track, non-inferiority only): corrected MAD22 and FRLL-Morphs cells that are diagnostic (best non-content morph-blind null below AUC 0.90): within 2 EER points of the best released detector, which must be scored through its own preprocessing with its published number reproduced within 3 points. Non-diagnostic cells are printed in grey under the null rows and never enter a headline mean.
Generator cells (MIPGAN, StyleGAN, MorDIFF, DiM): no state-of-the-art claim unless morph against one-identity render of the same generator reaches AUC 0.75 (lower bound above 0.65) on a generator not used in training. Otherwise the paper reports the measured limit and, if the author rules renders as manipulated, a separately named synthetic-render capability.

Shortcut-free means measured bounds, never a universal statement: (i) the paired score shift of genuine photos under each gated benign variant is within 0.25 genuine-score SD (equivalence test) and the flag rate changes by at most 5 points; (ii) the conflict cell (genuine photos more processed than the morphs) is within 0.05 AUC of the matched cell; (iii) the paired excess over the best morph-blind null has a lower bound above 0 on every claimed cell; (iv) the same recipe trained without any morph (AD4 data) stays at least 10 EER points worse than our detector on every claimed cell; (v) the score rises with the mixing fraction (Page p below 0.01) with at most half of the rise at the first step; (vi) with the face blanked the detector is at chance (folded AUC below 0.60) and with the background blanked it keeps at least 90% of its separation; (vii) expression-balanced and common-support re-reads move EER by less than 2 points; (viii) the cue table says what was not tested (print and scan, morph-side JPEG, colour).

REPORTING A LOSS ON BENCHMARKS THAT REWARD SHORTCUTS. Print both tracks in one table. Put the morph-blind rows on top (a network that never saw a morph: 0.0% on MorDIFF, 0.0 to 1.2% on DiM, 0.7 to 2.6% on three FRLL landmark cells). Give each detector a retention number: controlled separation divided by native separation. Show one scatter of native EER against controlled miss rate, where cue readers sit in the corner of good native and bad controlled results. State the expected sign of our native loss before scoring.

OPERATING POINTS. Miss rate at 5% and 10% false alarms on FRLL-size pools (204 photos cannot support 1%, which is two images). 1% only on pools of at least 3,000 genuine images from at least 300 persons (devbona 5,033; FRGC). Thresholds are transferred, never refit per cell. Flag rate on every rung. Person-clustered intervals with seeds nested. D-EER and AUC as secondary numbers for continuity. Names follow ISO/IEC 20059 and NIST (MACER at fixed BSCER); SYN-MAD style numbers go to the supplement.

CONTROLS A REVIEWER WILL DEMAND. History-matched genuine photos. A morph-side history swap (our same-pair morphs at tool size). Morph-free, label-permuted and untrained networks. A second genuine pool and an unseen source. Releases scored on their own preprocessing with reproduction shown. Recipe retrains with five or more seeds beside single released checkpoints. No test-set checkpoint selection for us, and a note where a comparator's code selects on test data (the SelfMAD code default). Expression-balanced subsets (11 of 17 cells are unbalanced). A common-support border mask. Same backbone and same image count with matched against unmatched data. The comparator recipe trained on our data. Frozen-backbone and zero-shot rows. Morph potency (share verifying against both contributors), results on potent morphs, and look-alike strata.

WHAT GETS THE PAPER REJECTED. A state-of-the-art claim that rests only on a test built to match our training. An audit of baselines whose published numbers we did not reproduce (AD1: the gate failed for every row). Evidence on 102 persons only. The word shortcut-free without bounds. Verdict cut-offs that look tuned after the fact, or shares above 1. A table where our detector loses every native cell with no null rows to explain it. No operating point. A method that is MADation plus our data presented as a new architecture. Calling a reconstruction genuine without saying so and without the alternative reading.
evaluation.detectability_analysis:
Landmark morphs (warp and alpha blend). Detectable in one image: (1) Blend trace. Averaging two aligned images scales independent sensor noise variance by alpha^2 + (1 - alpha)^2 (0.82 at mixing 0.1, 0.68 at 0.2, 0.50 at 0.5), so about 36% of the total drop is reached at 0.1: a smooth concave ramp, present equally in same-person morphs. In spliced morphs the unblended background of the same image is a built-in reference (noise SD ratio about 0.71 inside against outside at 0.5); a global resize or compression acts on both regions, so a within-image contrast is, to first order, independent of benign global processing. Full-frame or hull-only morphs lack that reference. (2) Ghost contours where the two faces do not coincide after the warp (iris, nostrils, lip line, hairline). These are larger for two persons than for two photos of one person, so this is the only part of the landmark signal that needs the second identity. (3) Piecewise-affine warp resampling. It is present in any warped image, including a warped genuine photo, so under the author's ruling it is not a morph signal; the current ladder cannot see it because the tools return the photo unchanged at mixing 0. Not detectable: which two people went in. After strong downscaling and compression the noise part fades and only ghosting at face scale remains; this matches the AMSL and WebMorph cells, where every history-robust network sits between 4 and 15% EER.

GAN latent morphs (MIPGAN, StyleGAN W+ average). The output is an ordinary sample of the generator, so every morph image is also a valid one-identity render. Detectable: (1) the generator trace, shared by every one-identity render; it is the whole benchmark signal today (camera photo against render AUC 0.90 to 1.00 for the three primary releases; render against morph at most 0.61 over 55 networks). (2) Averageness. With a population common component c0 and pair similarity c, the morph's cosine to the population centre grows by the factor sqrt(2 / (1 + c)): 1.38 for unrelated pairs, 1.15 for look-alikes at c = 0.5 (for example from 0.22 to 0.31 at c0 = 0.05). This is the only identity-level signal an ideal latent morph leaves. Naturally average faces and truncated one-identity renders have it too (the spread-matched control removes exactly this and gives 0.42 to 0.52), and benchmark pairs are chosen as look-alikes, the weak regime. A realistic expectation is AUC 0.55 to 0.70 at best, with false alarms concentrated on average-looking people. Not detectable: two identities as such.

Diffusion morphs (DiffAE, MorDIFF, DiM, Greedy-DiM). The same logic applies. (1) Decoder and sampler trace (step count, storage size), shared by reconstructions: the releases flag 20-step reconstructions at 82 to 99.5% and score them like morphs (0.40 to 0.49). (2) Mixing the two stochastic codes may superimpose fine detail of two images (hair, background), a blend-like trace that same-person mixes share; its size is unmeasured (reconstruction against same-person mix gives 0.27, 0.44 and 0.68 for the three releases, with no consistent sign). (3) Averageness of the semantic code, as for GANs. Greedy-DiM adds an identity-guided search whose trace is unknown. Not detectable so far: anything beyond the renderer.

Consequence for claims: a morph claim is realistic for landmark morphs (blend plus ghosting), a render claim for GAN and diffusion, and an averageness limit with a stated ceiling for latent morphs. These figures are derivations and expectations, not measurements.

ideas.title: 1. RungHeads: one backbone, one linear output per ladder step, fitted within host pairs, with a cross-talk matrix as the proof (recommended main line together with idea 3)
ideas.mechanism: Keep one network (CLIP ViT-L/14, MADation recipe). Give it up to four linear outputs, each fitted only on pairs that share the host photo and differ in exactly one ladder step: history (R0 vs R1), synthesis (R1 vs R2), mixing (R2 vs R3 and R4), second person (R3 vs R4). Fitting is within host (conditional logistic or paired ranking loss), so anything constant for a host (source, camera, frame, identity, expression) cannot enter a weight. The decision score is fixed in advance as the mixing output; the other outputs are printed as side information. The evidence is a cross-talk matrix: every output scored on every step, diagonal high, off-diagonal at 0.5.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Each output only ever sees a one-step difference inside a host, so pipeline, storage and source cannot be learned by it. The claim is then tested, not assumed: the mixing output must sit at 0.5 on R0 vs R1 (FRLL E7 pairs, FFHQ E7 pool) and on photo vs reconstruction (A43 arms E vs D20). It also survives either author ruling on generator reconstructions, because synthesis evidence has its own output and is reported separately.
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes, data are on disk now (AR1: 536 FRGC/FERET hosts x 2 tools, R0/R2/R3/R4/NC, plus 300 hosts x 6 mixing levels). Diffusion: known-generator only (DiffAE family; a 74-pair frozen head by Codex already reached 0.947 morph vs reconstruction on held-out FRGC dyads). GAN: only where twins exist (GAN32 64 blocks now, MIPGAN after AG1); expect weak. Cannot cover an unseen generator.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Tonight, frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 features, CPU heads. Fit on /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img/frgcferet (5-fold by host, leave one tool out), DiffAE train_fit blocks of /mnt/t7/smad_research/diffae-expanded123-v1, history pairs from /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a47/data47/i3 (render and its existing shrunk copy). Test with no refit on FRLL persons: AR1 img/frll and img/frll_bridge (published FRLL-Morphs pairs), A43 stored arms D20, C20, B20 and the 200 published MorDIFF morphs, FRLL E7 frames; and on /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/h1_poisson (598 pairs, unseen tool and unseen source).
ideas.falsifier: Mixing output R2 vs R4 on the held-out tool (FRLL persons) below 0.90; or H1 AUC not above 0.83 (best existing row, our MADation-recipe ViT-L/14; release 0.72); or any off-diagonal cell of the mixing output further than 0.10 from 0.5. For the diffusion claim: D20 vs B20 lower bound at or below 0.65 means no diffusion sentence.

ideas.title: 2. Null-space surgery: remove history directions estimated from paired differences, in closed form, from our head and from the released MADation heads
ideas.mechanism: Take pairs that differ only in processing history (a render or photo and its existing shrink-and-enlarge copy). Compute their feature differences at the layer that feeds the linear head, keep the top k principal directions (k fixed at 95% of difference energy on training pairs only), and subtract their span from the head weight. This is one matrix edit, no training, still one network. Applied to the released ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 heads it asks a sharp question: how much of their accuracy survives when the history direction is gone.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: The score cannot move along the estimated history directions to first order. It is checked with data not used for the estimate: E7 rise on FRLL cells and the six-rung dose ladder from A44 (release now +1.45 logits at dose 3.3, Spearman 1.0).
ideas.covers: History cue in all three families. It does not create a morph signal: generator cells fall to whatever is left (renderer trace or nothing). Useful as a component of idea 1 and as an audit row.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: 5,000 pairs from a47/data47/i3 (SMDD renders and copies made with prep_eval.degrade R 0.3125) for the estimate, the FFHQ E7 pool under /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a46 as a second estimate; never FRLL pairs. Rescore FRLL landmark and diffusion cells, native and E7, from cached penultimate features of the two MADation releases (AR1 scoring already writes feat_rel_madation_* files; the same extractor on the 14,120 eval frames). 30 to 60 minutes.
ideas.falsifier: After surgery the ViT-B/16 release still rises more than 5 points under E7 on MorDIFF (now +14.7) or DiM-C (now +23.1); or its FRLL FaceMorpher/OpenCV E7 error gets worse by more than 2 points (now 4.4/4.4); or the dose ladder still shows more than 0.3 logits at dose 3.3.
ideas.compute: Under 0.5 GPU-hour for features, the rest CPU.

If native diffusion numbers collapse, that is audit evidence, not a method win.

ideas.title: 3. SMDD-X: a history-crossed, pipeline-matched rebuild of the field's standard training set, same MADation recipe, all real pools held out
ideas.mechanism: The record says SMDD's two classes separate by one high-frequency scalar at AUC 0.99 or more, and I checked today that none of the 15,000 SMDD training morphs has a contributor among the 25,000 bona fide frames. Rebuild the morph class from the bona fide renders with the unchanged OpenCV and FaceMorpher tools, and cross history with label using only outputs that already exist: bona fide = render and its existing shrunk copy; morph = tool(render a, render b) and tool(copy a, copy b). Train the MADation recipe unchanged, last checkpoint, five seeds (ViT-B/16 first, where the E7 rise at the last checkpoint is +11.4; then ViT-L/14). Because training uses only synthetic identities, the whole FRGC/FERET ladder (536 hosts), H1 and FRLL are unseen persons and sources for this network.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: History is orthogonal to the label by design (2 x 2), and both classes share source, frame, size and storage. It is the standard SYN-MAD protocol, so against MADation only the data changed. This also fixes a gap in the plan: TwinSet is built from real photos, so any gain is confounded with 'trained on real photos' (the photos-only arm alone moved the E7 rise by 13 to 29 points).
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes. GAN and diffusion: no positive expected; a predicted loss of native diffusion accuracy for ViT-B/16 is causal audit evidence from the training side, which the paper lacks today.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Tonight on frozen CLIP features: head on SMDD as is vs head on SMDD-X (10,000 new morphs, about 5 minutes with the OpenCV tool at the measured 2,008 images per minute once landmark files exist). Compare E7 rise on the seven FRLL diffusion cells and four landmark cells, and R2 vs R4 on AR1. Thursday: 5 LoRA fits of the ViT-B/16 recipe (0.52 H100-hours each, measured in A47).
ideas.falsifier: SMDD-X ViT-B/16 at the last checkpoint still rises more than 4 points under E7 on the diffusion cells (reference +11.39 [8.00, 14.78] from 8 existing networks); or its FRLL FaceMorpher/OpenCV E7 error is more than 3 points worse than those 8 networks (3.6/5.8).
ideas.compute: CPU 1 to 2 hours (landmarks for 50,000 frames, then morphs). 2.6 H100-hours for 5 ViT-B/16 fits, about 10 for 5 ViT-L/14 fits; 5 to 15 USD if rented.

ideas.title: 4. Splice evidence maps: a patch head supervised by twin differences, scored against untouched patches of the same image
ideas.mechanism: For splice-type morphs (inner face blended into one host photo: AMSL, WebMorph, our H1 Poisson path) the morph and its host photo are pixel aligned, so the absolute difference gives a free label per patch: changed or untouched. Train a patch head on frozen ViT patch tokens with these labels. The image score is the mean of the top 10% patch logits minus the mean logit of the untouched ring (hair, background) of the same image.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Anything constant over the image (compression, resampling, source, sensor, generator) appears in both terms and cancels. The negatives are patches of the same file.
ideas.covers: Landmark splice morphs only, which are exactly the cells where the best release is weakest (AMSL 14.7%, WebMorph 4.4%, H1 AUC 0.72). Not full-frame morphs (the FaceMorpher path averages the backgrounds), not GAN, not diffusion (every patch is generated).
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: H1 (/mnt/t7/smad_heldout/h1_poisson, 598 morph and host pairs, orig and pp), 5-fold by CASIA person: patch head vs image-level head on the same tokens. Then zero-shot to the FRLL AMSL and WebMorph E7 frames. Patch tokens for about 6,000 images at 224 and 336 px input.
ideas.falsifier: FRLL AMSL error under E7 not below 10% (release 14.7%); or no gain of 0.03 AUC over the image-level head on H1 pp; or false alarms on E7 genuine photos up by more than 5 points.
ideas.compute: About 0.3 GPU-hour for tokens; heads on CPU. More training morphs with the approved h1_build.py on FRGC/FERET (CPU; throughput not verified).
ideas.main_risk: 14 px patches at 224 input are coarse, 336 is probably needed (2.25 x cost). H1 is small. A locally retouched genuine photo would be flagged.

ideas.title: 5. Mixing-direction test: is there one mixing direction across morph families? Paired directions, cosine matrix, leave-one-family-out
ideas.mechanism: For every family that has twins, compute the mean paired difference between a morph and its one-identity partner in frozen feature space, whitened by the within-pair covariance. Paired estimation removes host variance, so it is far more sample-efficient than the plain probes that failed at 16 to 90 pairs. Then print the cosine matrix between family directions with bootstrap intervals, and fit one pooled within-pair discriminant on all families but one and test it on the left-out family. One hour decides whether generator morphs can be covered by transfer at all.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Both members of a pair share generator, step count, storage and host, so the direction cannot encode them.
ideas.covers: Decides GAN and diffusion coverage. If directions agree (cosine above 0.3), a pooled head is justified. If not, the result is the measured limit for the fallback paper. Landmark is covered trivially.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Existing sets only: AR1 OpenCV and FaceMorpher (536 hosts each), diffae-expanded123 (102 complete blocks), GAN32 (64 blocks, vast-gan32 result folders), h4b_mipgan1 (338 pairs), h3_sg3 with the a37 spread-matched renders (423), and A43 on FRLL as test only. Features are the ones idea 1 needs anyway.
ideas.falsifier: For a transfer claim: leave-one-family-out AUC lower bound at or below 0.60 for DiffAE and for both StyleGAN sets, or all cross-family cosines below 0.2. Either number ends new GAN and diffusion training-data generation for this submission.

ideas.main_risk: H4b and H3 negatives are not full pipeline twins (render of the host, or of a third person). Small n per generator; a null can still be underpowered, so the bootstrap power is printed with it.

ideas.title: 6. Shape-by-texture factorial: a non-trivial 'tool on one photo' rung for landmark morphs, built from unchanged FaceMorpher calls
ideas.mechanism: tool(H, H) is bit-identical to the photo for OpenCV, so the landmark R2 rung carries no processing at all. graded_fm.py already calls the library's landmark averaging, warper and blender one by one. Call them with shape weight s and texture weight t in {0, 0.5}: (0, 0) the photo; (0.5, 0) the host warped toward a second photo of the same person, one texture; (0, 0.5) the partner's texture warped onto the host shape and averaged; (0.5, 0.5) the standard morph, which must reproduce the unchanged tool bit for bit. Use warp-only images as negatives in training and score all four cells for every detector.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: It separates 'was resampled by a piecewise warp' (processing) from 'two textures superimposed' (morphing) inside one tool with everything else equal. Without it, pipeline-matched landmark training is the same as the matched-source training the record already ran as d1.
ideas.covers: Landmark only.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Build 536 hosts x 4 cells in about 10 CPU minutes (this code path measured 432 images per minute), verify the (0.5, 0.5) cell against the existing m = 0.5 graded images, score with the AR1 scorer and the heads of idea 1.
ideas.falsifier: A detector with (0.5, 0) vs (0, 0) AUC above 0.65 reads the warp. Our head trained with warp-only negatives must keep (0.5, 0.5) vs (0.5, 0) at 0.90 or more and (0.5, 0) vs (0, 0) within 0.10 of 0.5.
ideas.compute: CPU only; scoring minutes.

The library averages backgrounds (bg = weighted_average(h, b)); the background rule must be the same in all four cells or it becomes the cue. A warp toward same-person geometry is small, so the control may be weak.

ideas.title: 7. Cue spectrometer: use the step outputs as an instrument on benchmark cells and on released detectors (for the fallback paper)

For each cell report how well each output alone separates the published classes. For each released detector regress its logit on the three outputs and report the share explained by each. This complements the interventional ladder with a learned attribution and needs no new image.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: It is an audit tool, not a detector. Its validity is anchored on cells where an intervention already gave the answer.
ideas.covers: All benchmark cells of all three families, as audit. No detection claim.

State of the art, operationally: the reference protocol is the history-matched one, declared before scoring. (a) On corrected MAD22 and FRLL-based cells with E7 genuine photos, mean and worst-cell error (EER, and false alarms at 5% missed attacks) not worse than the best released detector, with a paired person-bootstrap interval; the bar to beat today is the MADation ViT-L/14 release at about 1.0 / 1.0 / 14.7 / 4.4% on FRLL landmark families. (b) On the ladder, the verdict 'reads morphing' for landmark morphs on a held-out tool and an unseen source (H1 above 0.83). (c) Native landmark cells within 2 points of the best release. pragmatist.detectability_analysis:
Landmark morphs. Detectable in one image: superposition of two warped textures (double contours at iris, nostrils, lips, eyebrows). Its strength should scale with the cross term 4a(1-a): 36% of maximum at mixing 0.1, 84% at 0.3, 100% at 0.5, which the existing graded set can test. Also a loss of uncorrelated fine detail by the factor a^2 + (1-a)^2 (0.5 at a = 0.5, 0.58 at 0.3, 0.82 at 0.1), but that is confounded with blur and resampling and must not be the cue. Present in same-person morphs too, so R2 vs R3 should already be high. The second person adds only larger ghosting where shapes differ, confounded with session gap. Not detectable: who the contributors are, or a two-person morph of look-alikes vs a same-person morph in the limit of equal faces.

GAN latent morphs. An ideal generator's midpoint is a valid single face. What remains is a shift toward the latent centre: the predicted norm factor sqrt((1+c)/2) is 0.77 for c near 0.2, and the record's H3 numbers (median distance from the mean latent 35.9 for morphs vs 46.7 for renders, ratio 0.77) match it for c of about 0.18. A frozen probe reads this at 0.91 in-generator (A38), and it vanishes against spread-matched renders (0.42 to 0.52). So the only single-image signal is typicality, with a ceiling that falls toward chance for look-alike pairs and average-looking genuine faces. MIPGAN optimisation traces against the A = B control are unknown until AG1.

Diffusion (DiffAE family). Mixing two stochastic codes destroys image-specific detail; this mixing trace is present in same-person and two-person morphs and absent in a one-photo reconstruction. In-generator it is learnable with tiny data (0.947 on FRGC, Codex) and it does not transfer to GAN (0.26 to 0.52). All released detectors sit at 0.40 to 0.49 on reconstruction vs morph (AD1) and flag 82 to 99% of reconstructions at the benchmark threshold. Second identity inside diffusion morphs: 0.65 to 0.86 in-generator, confounded by expression and pose gap.

Across families: no evidence yet for a shared signal. Idea 5 measures it in an hour.

ideas.title: 1. Blend-evidence maps: dense supervision with the measured two-source disagreement
ideas.mechanism: We own the landmark tools, so for every morph we can save the two warped source faces and compute where they actually disagree: D = |warped A minus warped B|, averaged per ViT patch. D is zero for a tool run on one photo, small for a same-person morph and large for a two-person morph. A small head on patch tokens regresses this map and the image score is the mean of the top 10 percent of predicted patches; camera photos, their shrink-and-enlarge (E7) copies and one-photo tool outputs are trained with all-zero maps. This transplants Face X-ray, LAA-Net and Forensics Adapter (blending-boundary maps as supervision) to S-MAD, but with exact targets instead of synthetic masks. Backbone frozen first, then LayerNorm-only tuning (the GenD recipe) or LoRA.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: (a) The target changes inside one image while file history is constant inside one image, so history alone cannot fit it. (b) Uniform softness (E7 copies) is taught as zero, local two-source disagreement as positive; this is the physical difference between resampling blur and blend blur. (c) The same host appears with a same-person partner and a two-person partner with different maps, so face content alone cannot fit it. (d) It gives a validity check no file cue can pass: correlation between predicted and true maps on a held-out tool, and collapse when the face is blanked. Honest limit: a head could still learn 'anatomy prior times a global morph flag'; idea 7 measures exactly that.
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes (OpenCV, FaceMorpher, the approved Poisson warp path; same-person morphs get a graded target, which matches the author ruling that they are morphs). GAN and diffusion: no, there is no pixel-level two-source target; the head should stay near zero there, which is why idea 2 exists.

ideas.title: 2. Regeneration evidence under a history-matched contrast, with two reporting protocols (B-Free and DDA transplant)
ideas.mechanism: For GAN and diffusion morphs the record shows nobody separating a morph from a one-identity render of the same generator (today's AD1: 0.40 to 0.49 for all releases; AG5: best of 55 networks 0.61), and small trained heads did not transfer between generators. What is reliably in the image is that the face was re-synthesised by a decoder. Train a second evidence head on pairs made the B-Free way: a camera photo with history h against the same photo's reconstruction with the same history h, so content, identity and expression are identical and only the decoder differs. Report every generator cell under two protocols: S (strict, a one-photo reconstruction is genuine; expected near chance and stated as a measured limit) and O (operational, any regenerated face is rejected).
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Both classes come from the same photo, so source, pose, expression and framing carry no label information. The photo's own E7 copy is an explicit negative, so 'looks resampled' cannot be the cue; DDA's lesson is applied by storing both members through the same storage path. The ladder then has to show the head flat on R0 to R1 and high on R1 to R2. It deliberately uses the renderer fingerprint, so it is shortcut-free only under protocol O. NEEDS THE RULING: 'one-photo reconstruction counts as manipulated'. If the ruling is 'processed genuine', this idea supplies only the limit statement and a hard negative class.
ideas.covers: GAN: yes under protocol O. Diffusion: yes under protocol O. Landmark: no. Under protocol S it covers nothing, by design.

ideas.title: 3. Positive-evidence-only scoring with typed heads inside one network (Stay-Positive transplant)
ideas.mechanism: The E7 failure is a detector raising its score when camera detail disappears. Stay-Positive fixes the same shape of problem in generated-image detection by retraining only the last layer with non-negative weights on non-negative features, so no feature can vote for 'genuine' and the absence of real-image traces cannot raise the score. For S-MAD: the final score is a noisy-OR of two non-negative evidence heads in one network (blend evidence from idea 1, regeneration evidence from idea 2). The first step needs no new data: refit only the last layer of the released MADation networks and of our M3/M3L retrains (last checkpoint) on SMDD with the constraint, using the fixed post-activation units of the last transformer MLP as the non-negative features.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: It removes one named mechanism by construction (features that mean 'this is a camera photo'), not every shortcut: 'resampled softness present' can still be learned as positive evidence, so it must be paired with history negatives. Typed heads make each kind of evidence auditable on the ladder: the blend head must be flat on R0, R1, R2 and rise only at R3/R4 of landmark tools; the regeneration head must be flat on R0 to R1.
ideas.covers: Scoring rule for all three families; by itself it adds no new signal for any of them. It cannot create identity reading for GAN or diffusion.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Features of the released MADation ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 (weights in /mnt/t7/wcss_backups/madation_official_upload/) on the 40,000 SMDD training images, the FRLL bench frames native and E7 for the 7 diffusion and 4 landmark cells, and the A43 arms. Fit two last layers per network on SMDD: unconstrained logistic and non-negative logistic. Read: E7 rise per cell, R0 vs R1 AUC on the MorDIFF ladder (today 0.894 for ViT-B/16, 0.645 for ViT-L/14), native EER.
ideas.falsifier: For the ViT-B/16 features the MorDIFF E7 rise must fall below +7.4 points (half of the released +14.7); kill if it does not, or if the native mean EER over the 17 cells rises by more than 3 points.
ideas.compute: About 0.3 GPU-h of feature extraction on the DGX, minutes of fitting.
ideas.main_risk: Softness is encoded as a positive feature and the constraint changes nothing. ViT features are not naturally 'present or absent' the way rectified CNN features are, so the published recipe may not carry over. The released ViT-L/14 has no E7 rise in EER to remove, so the demonstration rests on ViT-B/16 and the retrains.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Stay-Positive (Sundara Rajan and Lee, ICML 2025, arXiv 2502.07778, checked by search this session). In S-MAD I found nothing with a positive-only constraint; one-class methods (SPL-MAD, SRL-MAD) do the opposite and model only the genuine class, which is exactly the class whose appearance depends on processing. Transplant looks novel for MAD (not exhaustive).

ideas.title: 4. History-null constrained adaptation and a stopping rule validated on shortcuts, not on benchmarks
ideas.mechanism: We hold exact history pairs: a photo and its E7 copy, an SMDD render and its shrunk copy, the six-rung dose ladder of A44. Their paired feature differences span the directions in which processing history moves the features. Project the top k of these directions out before the head (nuisance projection, a linear erasure), and when adapting with LayerNorm-only or LoRA keep the update in the complement, as Effort does for a subspace chosen by SVD. Fix adaptation depth and training length in advance by a shortcut metric on non-FRLL data (R0 vs R1 AUC at most 0.55), because in the record the same MADation recipe goes from 34.7 to 4.4 percent MorDIFF EER between the early and the last checkpoint and gains an E7 rise of +11.4 on the way.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: For a linear head on projected features the score cannot move along the removed directions, by construction. The guarantee is linear only and holds only for the histories we measured. The stopping rule prevents choosing the checkpoint whose benchmark gain is the shortcut; it is fixed on data that contains no FRLL person.
ideas.covers: All three families as cue removal; it adds no detection signal. Most relevant where adapted networks follow history (diffusion cells).
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Directions from FFHQ native and resolution-matched pairs (A46 pool) and /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a47/data47 pairs, on CLIP ViT-L/14 and DINOv3 features, k = 4, 16, 64. Refit the linear head on SMDD and on the C pool; test on FRLL: E7 rise on the 7 diffusion and 4 landmark cells, a fresh MLP probe for native vs E7 photos on the projected features (folds by person), native EER. Zero-GPU part: from the existing score files of the 8 M3 and 5 M3L retrains at es.pt and last.pt, tabulate benchmark EER against E7 rise per checkpoint to show the trade-off the stopping rule acts on.
ideas.falsifier: Kill if, after removing at most 64 directions, the fresh probe still separates FRLL native from E7 photos at AUC above 0.75, or the E7 rise is not at least halved, or native mean EER rises by more than 3 points.
ideas.compute: Minutes on cached features; zero GPU for the checkpoint table.
ideas.main_risk: The closest earlier attempt (per-image token normalisation) failed with the cue still decodable. History is unlikely to be a small linear subspace. The frozen CLIP probe already has an E7 rise near 0 (A12: -0.2, -3.2, -0.5), so any gain shows only for adapted models. Blend softness and resampling softness share directions, so the projection can remove the landmark signal.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Effort (Yan et al., ICML 2025, arXiv 2411.15633) and GenD (Yermakov et al., WACV 2026, arXiv 2508.06248), both checked via local review notes; NS-Net (arXiv 2508.01248, checked by search this session: projects CLIP image features onto the null space of text features to remove semantics); LEACE (NeurIPS 2023, memory); nuisance attribute projection in speaker verification (memory). S-MAD: R-FLoRA (Ramachandra, TIFS 2026, arXiv 2604.17321, checked via local note and search) goes the other way and feeds residual statistics into the adaptation. A null space estimated from paired processing copies was not found in MAD.

ideas.title: 5. History-symmetric self-blending, with an SMDD-only variant built from mirror self-morphs
ideas.mechanism: SelfMAD's released recipe blends each photo with a resampled zoom of itself and never resamples the genuine partner (record note), so 'resampled' is tied to 'attack' and the release collapses under E7 (Greedy-DiM 8.4 to 90.7). Keep the self-supervised idea but make it symmetric: the genuine and the attack share the same processing, and the only difference is that the attack averages two different warped copies. Within our tool rules: tool(A, A) is the genuine image; tool(A, mirror of A) and tool(A, second photo of A) are one-person morphs; tool(A, B) is the two-person morph. Mirroring is an index reversal, not resampling, so SMDD (one image per synthetic identity) gets same-identity morphs without any generator, and the dense targets of idea 1 come for free.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: The label is decoupled from resampling by construction, and every identity appears under every label. The SMDD-only variant keeps the field's training protocol, which answers the reviewer question 'is the gain your data or your method' with the standard data.
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes. GAN and diffusion: no (SelfMAD's frequency patterns are a regeneration cue and belong to idea 2).
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: (a) No training, tonight, CPU minutes: build tool(A, mirror A) with the unchanged OpenCV and FaceMorpher tools for the 536 AR1 hosts and the 102 FRLL persons, and check with the released detectors and a frozen-feature probe whether mirror self-morphs behave like the existing two-photo twins R3 (AUC mirror vs R3 inside 0.40 to 0.60). (b) About 1 GPU-h: frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 head trained on SMDD only (SMDD genuine images, tool morphs of SMDD pairs, mirror self-morphs, built on CPU for about 5,000 identities), compared with the usual SMDD head on the four FRLL landmark cells native and E7 and on the AR1 held-out twins.
ideas.falsifier: Kill the SMDD-only variant if its mean E7 rise over the four FRLL landmark cells exceeds 3 points, or its AMSL EER under E7 exceeds 19.7 percent (5 points worse than the released MADation ViT-L/14 at 14.7).
ideas.compute: CPU 1 to 2 h for the SMDD builds, about 1 GPU-h for features and heads; LayerNorm-only fits about 5 GPU-h for 5 seeds.
ideas.main_risk: A mirror self-morph is an unnaturally symmetric face, which is a content cue, not ghosting; it must never be the only one-person morph in training. SMDD is 256 px, so fine blend detail is missing. SMDD genuine images are GAN renders, which conflicts with protocol O of idea 2.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Self-Blended Images (CVPR 2022, memory); SelfMAD (Ivanovska et al., FG 2025, arXiv 2504.05504, checked by search this session); SelfMAD++ (Ivanovska Preskar, Todorov, Peer, Struc, Information Fusion 2026, seen only as a citation inside the SRL-MAD page opened this session); the 'alpha blending' deepfake paper is withdrawn and must not be cited for numbers. History symmetry and mirror twins were not found in MAD.

ideas.title: 6. Local evidence at native scale: fixed interior crops in place of one shrunk whole frame
ideas.mechanism: Shrinking the 512 frame to 224 keeps only the lowest 44 percent of its frequency band. The discarded band holds the resampling history and also most of the blend softness, which may be why CLIP at 224 barely moves under E7 and yet stays at 14.7 to 17.7 percent on AMSL. Give the same single network K fixed 224-pixel crops cut from the 512 frame without resizing (eyes, nose, mouth, cheeks, hairline) and pool the crop scores with a top-k mean. Interior crops cannot see zero borders, canvas or background. Native scale makes history visible again, so this only makes sense together with history negatives in training.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: It removes three measured cues by construction: border fraction (alone AUC 0.99 to 1.00 on several landmark cells), canvas and colour statistics (0.71 to 1.00 on aligned crops, today's C3), and background. Leaving out the mouth crop gives an expression-blind variant (the expression label alone reaches 0.75 in 11 of 17 cells, today's C1).
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes, aimed at AMSL and WebMorph. GAN and diffusion: only as an input option for idea 2. It does not create identity reading.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Same AR1 feature pass as idea 1 with three inputs per image: whole frame at 224, whole frame at 336, five native 224 crops. Same image-level head and folds. Read: held-out-tool R3 vs R4 AUC, FRLL AMSL and WebMorph EER native and E7 (existing frames), false-alarm rate on R1f, and the AR3 non-content baselines beside it.
ideas.falsifier: Kill if native crops do not raise held-out-tool R3 vs R4 AUC by at least 0.05 over the whole frame at 224, or if with history negatives they raise the mean E7 rise on the four FRLL landmark cells by more than 5 points.
ideas.compute: About 1 GPU-h on the DGX (five times the feature cost of the whole frame).
ideas.main_risk: Pooling several crops of one image through one network may be read as an ensemble: needs the author's ruling. A face-region restriction was already tried on GAN twins and failed against spread-matched controls (different purpose, but a warning). SMDD upsampled from 256 px has no native detail, so this needs real-photo training pools.
ideas.closest_prior_work: B-Free: native 504-pixel crops, no resizing, crop logits averaged (CVPR 2025, checked via local review note); SAFE crop-not-resize and patch-shuffle detectors (memory); R-FLoRA uses CLIP at 336 (checked via local note); MADation resizes the whole face to 224 (checked by search). Low novelty alone; useful as a factor in the first experiment.

ideas.title: 7. Planted-confound stress test: a recipe-level certificate of shortcut resistance
ideas.mechanism: Matched data shows that a detector had no shortcut available; it does not show that the method resists one when it is available. Train each recipe on data in which a known nuisance is tied to the label with strength 0, 0.5, 0.8 and 1.0, test on matched data, and report the loss of matched-test AUC as a susceptibility index of the recipe. Nuisances come only from existing approved outputs: the identically post-processed 'pp' variant against 'orig' in the H1 set, E7 against native copies, 20-step against 100-step DiffAE renders in A43.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: It is a measurement, not a mitigation: it turns 'our data are matched' into 'our training rule ignores a planted cue of known strength', and ranks image-level labels, dense maps (idea 1), positive-only heads (idea 3), history-null (idea 4) and frozen vs LayerNorm-only vs LoRA on one scale. It also answers the reviewer question 'what happens if someone retrains your method on SMDD'.
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes (H1 pp/orig, E7). Diffusion: yes with the step-count nuisance (FRLL persons, so evaluation only by cross-validation and reported as an audit). GAN: not with current assets.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/h1_poisson/data: 598 pairs, morph and host photo, each as orig and pp. Frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 features, 5 folds by pair, four confound strengths, heads: image-level logistic and the dense head of idea 1 (targets from the script's own warped images, saved by a verified re-run). Test always on pp vs pp and orig vs orig.
ideas.falsifier: If the image-level head loses less than 0.05 matched AUC at full confound, the planted cue is too weak to be a test and the set is dropped. If every recipe loses more than 80 percent of its above-chance AUC at full confound, the index does not discriminate recipes and the idea is only an audit figure.
ideas.compute: Minutes on the DGX once features exist (about 2,400 images).
ideas.main_risk: The pp nuisance (unsharp mask, colour transfer, JPEG 85 to 95) may be invisible to CLIP at 224. H1 sources are 112-pixel crops upsampled to 512. The index describes heads on frozen features, not full fine-tuning.
ideas.closest_prior_work: 'Fake or JPEG' controlled-bias audit (ECCVW 2024, taken from the local literature note, not opened by me); AVH-Align silence-trimming audit (CVPR 2025, arXiv 2412.00175, checked via local review note); Waterbirds-style spurious-correlation benchmarks (memory). Nothing of this kind was found for MAD.

objections_to_current_plan: The 'pipeline-matched genuine' class is empty for landmark tools. AR1's own smoke test says OpenCV run on one photo is bit-identical to the input and FaceMorpher differs by at most 1 grey level in 14 percent of pixels. So TwinMAD's main training contrast is 'untouched frame against morph', nothing in training says 'soft or resampled is not a morph', and the R0 to R1 step is zero by construction on our builds. A TwinMAD network can therefore still flag E7 photos on the benchmarks. Training needs history negatives at several doses, and the same doses on morphs.

The 'reads morphing' rule (R2 vs R4 at least 0.75 and R0 to R2 share at most 0.2) is trivially half-satisfied for landmark tools because R2 equals R0. Add R1 vs R4, and the false-alarm rate on R1 and R2 at a fixed threshold. That rate is the author ruling written as a number; today it is 51 to 98 percent for E7 photos and 82 to 99.5 percent for reconstructions (AD1).

For generators the plan spends its largest budget (D3, D4: 35 GPU-h for audit sets, 150 for training sets) on the contrast that is already at chance for every release (AD1 0.40 to 0.49; AG5 best of 55 networks 0.61) and where trained heads did not transfer across generators. The author objected twice to time spent on generation. The decision that actually changes the generator half of the paper is the open ruling on one-photo reconstructions, and it costs nothing.

The baseline to beat is weaker than fact 2 suggests. Today's AD1 shows the released MADation ViT-L/14 also 'reads the benchmark' on MorDIFF: R0 vs R1 0.645, R1 vs R2 0.743, R2 vs R4 0.486, 51 percent of E7 photos flagged at its benchmark threshold, and 26.0 percent EER on the sampled cell. 'Does not move under E7' is true for its Greedy-DiM EER only.

Image-level labels only. A positive TwinMAD result will show that features separate the classes, not what they read; the readability probe has the same weakness. A dense target (idea 1) gives evidence a file cue cannot fake.

'Last checkpoint, fixed recipe' is not neutral. In A44 the same recipe is at 34.7 percent MorDIFF EER at the early checkpoint and 4.4 at the last, with the E7 rise appearing in between. Training length should be fixed by a shortcut metric on non-FRLL data, before any benchmark is read.

Input scale is an untested factor. Whole frame at 224 discards the top 56 percent of the band; that probably protects against history and also hides blend softness (AMSL 14.7 to 17.7 percent). The plan has no 224 / 336 / native-crop arm.

Expression is a live cue in 11 of 17 cells (morphs all neutral, genuine class half smiling, 0.75 by the label alone, today's C1). Benchmark numbers for every detector, ours included, should also be given on the neutral-only genuine subset; this costs nothing.

The dose test expects a ramp. Blend physics says the high-frequency energy of a blend is 1 - 2a(1-a)(1-rho) of the source energy, so 84 percent of the full effect is already reached at mixing 0.3. A flat curve between 0.3 and 0.5 is legitimate and must not be read as 'pipeline cue'.
The plan leaves the field's SMDD-only training protocol with no SMDD-only row. Reviewers will ask whether the gain is the data or the method. Idea 5 gives an SMDD-only variant on CPU.

Related work is behind: SelfMAD++ (2026), the PADLLM/MADLLM study (Aug 2026, LoRA CLIP ViT-L/14 as a strong baseline over 30 encoders), R-FLoRA (TIFS 2026) and NIST FATE MORPH (Sept 2026) are not in the comparison set of the plan.

adjacent.detectability_analysis:
What one image can and cannot show, per family. Numbers are from the record unless marked as my reasoning.

LANDMARK (pixel blend of two warped photos).
- Detectable 1, blend softness: for a blend M = (1-a)A + aB, a frequency band with equal power in both sources and correlation rho keeps the fraction 1 - 2a(1-a)(1-rho) of its power (my derivation). Two different faces, fine texture, a = 0.5: half the power (3 dB). The effect is 0.18, 0.32, 0.42, 0.48, 0.50 for a = 0.1 to 0.5, so it saturates early.
- Detectable 2, ghosting: a second, weaker copy of misaligned edges (iris rim, nostrils, lips, hairline), contrast about min(a, 1-a). It is local and mid-frequency, so it survives a shrink to 224.
- Detectable 3: splice seam or Poisson boundary, tool-specific.
- Key consequence: skin micro-texture of two sessions of ONE person is also uncorrelated at pixel level (rho near 0), so a same-person morph loses the same fine detail as a two-person morph. Same-person and two-person morphs can differ only in mid-frequency feature-shape disagreement. Prediction: tool-on-one-photo vs morph is easy; same-person vs two-person morph is moderate and falls for look-alike pairs.
- Confusable with processing: uniform resampling blur removes the same band. The only principled separation is spatial: blend softness sits where two sources disagree, resampling softness is uniform. This is the reason for dense targets (idea 1).
- Not detectable so far: the second identity as such (image-only probes failed to read it, H-new-318). Typicality is weak: the mean of two identity vectors shrinks by sqrt((1+c)/2), 0.71 for unrelated pairs, 0.79 at the AR1 partner cosine of 0.23, 0.87 for look-alikes at 0.5.
- Record: CLIP-based rows reach 0.72 to 0.87 zero-shot on the clean H1 set (file-size floor 0.62). Whether they read blend or border/colour is open: border fraction alone gives 0.99 to 1.00 and colour statistics 0.97 to 0.98 on the FRLL FaceMorpher and OpenCV cells.

GAN (latent mixing, MIPGAN, StyleGAN).
- Detectable: the renderer fingerprint against camera photos (0.90 to 0.97, already in frozen CLIP at 0.92). Every one-identity render carries it too. It counts only if the author rules a reconstruction 'manipulated'.
- Detectable but not a morph signal: latent centrality; it vanishes against spread-matched renders (0.42 to 0.52, 11 of 12 upper bounds below 0.5).
- Not detectable on current evidence: two-identity render against one-identity render. Best of 55 networks 0.61; trained small heads reach 0.73 to 0.78 inside one generator against reconstructions and reverse on another generator (0.26 to 0.32), with only 16 training pairs.
- Unknown: whether the MIPGAN optimiser leaves its own trace when run with A = B (AG1 will show).

DIFFUSION (DiffAE, DiM, MorDIFF).
- Detectable: decoder and step-count trace (R1 vs R2: 0.917 ViT-B/16, 0.743 ViT-L/14) and the small storage size of the published files (history, not allowed).
- Not detectable on current evidence: reconstruction against morph. All releases 0.40 to 0.49 (AD1); the sign of 'reconstruction vs same-person mix' differs between detectors (0.27 for ViT-B/16, 0.68 for SelfMAD), so there is no stable interpolation trace zero-shot.
- A symmetric history treatment removed 89 percent of the E7 rise for the Inception recipe and cost 52 EER points on the diffusion cells: for that network the history was the performance.

BOTTOM LINE. Landmark: positive, local, physically grounded evidence exists and can be supervised densely. GAN and diffusion: the only reliable single-image evidence is regeneration; identity mixing is not readable today. A paper that claims state of the art on generator morphs must either get the 'manipulated' ruling and report an operational protocol next to a strict one, or state the limit.

Note (my inference, not a result): a 512 frame shrunk to 224 keeps 44 percent of the band, which would explain why whole-frame CLIP is robust to E7 and weak on AMSL at the same time. ViT-B/16 at the same input size does move under E7, so this is not the whole story.
adjacent.sota_definition:
STATE OF THE ART, operational definition.
One network, five seeds (mean and spread), training length fixed in advance, thresholds set on development data without FRLL persons. For every cell (corrected MAD22 x 5, FRLL-Morphs x 5, MorDIFF, DiM x 6) report EER and the bona fide error at 5 and 1 percent missed morphs, for three genuine pools: native photos (R0), history-matched photos (R1, the existing E7 frames) and, on generator cells, one-photo reconstructions (R2). The headline per cell is the WORSE of native and E7. The claim holds if the mean of these worst-case errors is below that of the best released detector scored the same way, with a paired person-bootstrap interval excluding 0, and no family is worse by more than 2 points. Reference today: released MADation ViT-L/14 under E7, FRLL FaceMorpher / OpenCV / AMSL / WebMorph 1.0 / 1.0 / 14.7 / 4.4, Greedy-DiM 9.8. Native-only numbers of other methods are printed but are not the bar, since they can collapse under E7 (SelfMAD Greedy-DiM 8.4 to 90.7).
Generator cells are reported under two protocols: S (strict: reconstruction of one photo is genuine) and O (operational: any regenerated face is rejected). Which one is the headline is the author's ruling.

SHORTCUT-FREE, operational definition (all on data with no training person):
1. History: R0 vs R1 AUC inside 0.45 to 0.55 on FRLL and on one non-FRLL pool; false-alarm rate on R1 (and on R2 for landmark tools) within 2 points of the rate on R0 at the operating threshold.
2. Beats the best non-content baseline (file attributes, border mask, background only), paired lower bound above 0.
3. Face blanked: AUC at most 0.60. Background blanked: AUC loss at most 0.05.
4. Neutral-only genuine subset within 2 points of the full cell.
5. Dose: score rises with mixing level (Page test); on a held-out tool the predicted evidence map correlates with the true disagreement map (median Spearman at least 0.30).
6. Planted-confound index (idea 7) reported for the recipe.
No universal 'free of all cues' claim; the cue table lists what was tested.
