ideas.title: Identity-subspace shrinkage test (ISS): a detector fitted on genuine photos only
ideas.mechanism: Every morph is a midpoint in a generative identity space: with contributor correlation c, identity variance falls to (1+c)/2 of a real person's, whether the average is taken on landmarks and pixels, on StyleGAN codes or on DiffAE semantic codes. Fit, on genuine multi-session photos only, the within-person covariance S_w and between-person covariance S_b of one frozen backbone's features, whiten by S_w and keep the directions where persons differ more than sessions do. The score is the Gaussian likelihood ratio 'midpoint of two people' against 'one capture' (a weighted squared norm, small means morph); a second read-out on session-dominated directions catches same-person mixes, where session variance halves and identity does not. Arms with the same statistic: DiffAE semantic code (512-d, zero mean and unit variance by design), CLIP ViT-L/14, DINOv3, glintr100 as gallery density, and Procrustes-aligned 106-point landmarks (a pixel-blind arm). The fit also gives a predicted AUC before any morph is seen: Phi(sqrt(d/2)*(1-s)/sqrt(1+s^2)) with s = ((1+c)/2+n)/(1+n), d the effective identity dimension and n the session-to-identity variance ratio.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: No morph and no render is used to fit it, so no label can attach to a pipeline. Whitening by S_w suppresses the directions along which one person changes between sessions, cameras and compressions, which is where processing history lives; the landmark arm cannot see pixels at all. The record already shows a glintr100 probe clean on both history controls (native vs E7 0.506, reconstruction vs aligner-only 0.493; A46 d2). It still has to pass its own null: genuine R0 vs R1 AUC inside 0.45 to 0.55.
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes (the shape average is exact in landmark space; texture average approximate). GAN: yes in principle (latent averaging is this effect; H3 probes read it at 0.91) but only the identity part counts as morph evidence. Diffusion: yes in principle (z_sem interpolation is this effect). Cannot cover: look-alike pairs (c above about 0.6 gives a predicted ceiling near 0.65 at d = 30), same-person GAN or diffusion mixes (identity part unchanged), and it will flag any one-person image pulled toward the mean face (truncated render, strong beautification). It needs no ruling on reconstructions: an identity-preserving reconstruction scores as genuine.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Fit S_w and S_b on FRGC and colorFERET persons outside the AR1 pool (the 663 persons AF0 lists; val10 excluded by the prep_train.is_val rule). Step 1, CPU, 5 minutes: landmark arm from existing .tem files of /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1 (R0 = tem_H, R3 = mean of tem_H and tem_S, R4 = mean of tem_H and tem_B, dose = (1-m)*tem_H + m*tem_B); this is the exact-geometry upper bound. Step 2: glintr100 arm from the embeddings gate G-b computes for AR1 rungs (pool_src_emb.npz plus rung embeddings). Step 3, under 30 GPU-minutes: DiffAE encoder, CLIP-L and DINOv3 features for a43 stored sets (E 204, D20 204, C20 102, B20 200, published A 200), AR1 OpenCV and FaceMorpher rungs (R0, R2w, R3, R3m, R4, NC, 536 each), the FaceMorpher graded set m000 to m050 (300 hosts), h3_sg3 (423 + 423), GAN32 blocks, and FRLL native vs existing E7 frames. Print per arm: R0 vs R1, R2 vs R4, R3 vs R4, R2 vs R3, dose trend, and predicted vs observed AUC. My rough predictions (estimates): exact-landmark arm R0 vs R4 0.75 to 0.85; glintr100 arm 0.60 to 0.70; DiffAE z_sem arm on D20 vs B20 at least 0.80.
ideas.falsifier: Best arm R2-vs-R4 AUC below 0.65 on both a43 (D20 vs B20) and AR1 (R2w vs R4, OpenCV); or genuine R0 vs R1 (FRLL E7 frames) AUC outside 0.40 to 0.60; or no monotone rise over m000 to m050 (Page p above 0.05). For the exact-landmark arm alone: R0 vs R4 below 0.60 kills shape shrinkage.

ideas.title: Ghost-energy target: regress the foreign layer, not the mixing fraction (upgrade of AF0)
ideas.mechanism: In a pixel blend I = (1-a)*wA + a*wB the mixing fraction a is not identifiable where the two warped layers agree (smooth skin on both): blending there leaves no trace at any a. What is physically in the image is the foreign layer a*(wB - wA). Replace AF0's nominal target a(x) by the ghost energy per patch, g = 4*a*(1-a)*std_patch(wA - wB), divided by the patch's own contrast. It is zero for every one-capture image whatever its warp or history, small for same-person blends in the inner face, large for two-person blends, and grows with dose. Image score = mean or upper quantile of predicted g inside the face hull.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: The target varies inside the image and is exactly zero for all single-capture images, so no image-constant cue predicts it. Unlike alpha, it cannot be predicted from 'this region is smooth': smooth agreeing regions have target zero at any alpha, so the head is not taught that softness means mixing. Benign blur then lowers the score (a miss) and does not raise it (the forbidden false alarm on a processed genuine photo). Check: genuine score shift R0 to R1 at most 0.3 SD.
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes, all tools, including the blended interior of splice morphs. Same-person landmark morphs: partly (hair, collar, expression differences between sessions are real ghost energy; consistent with the ruling that they are morphs). GAN and diffusion: no, there is no pixel superposition; predicted null, which is itself a clean statement of non-coverage.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: AF0 already has wA and wB inside af_morph.warped_pair. Add the per-patch statistic to the map it saves (numpy only, no image written), rebuild wave 1 (about 700 images, CPU minutes), refit the ridge and MLP heads on the DINOv3-L/16 at 512 and CLIP-L/14 at 336 patch features AF0 extracts anyway. Compare ghost-target and alpha-target heads on: within-image rank correlation (AF0 F1), AR1 FaceMorpher and OpenCV R2w vs R4, R3 vs R4, NC vs R3, the graded set m000 to m050, FRLL E7 shift (AF0 F3), and FRLL-Morphs AMSL and WebMorph against the released MADation ViT-L/14 (14.7 and 4.4 percent EER under E7).
ideas.falsifier: Ghost head R2w-vs-R4 AUC below 0.75 on AR1 FaceMorpher; or genuine R0 to R1 shift above 0.3 SD; or it is neither at least 0.03 AUC better than the alpha head on R3 vs R4 nor lower in E7 shift.
ideas.compute: CPU rebuild 10 to 20 minutes; heads in minutes; no GPU beyond the features AF0 already extracts.
ideas.main_risk: At 16-pixel patches ghost energy is dominated by the periphery (hair outline, collar), where two photos always differ, so the head may become a 'double outline' detector; splice morphs (AMSL) remove that evidence and leave only the weak inner-face ghost. Report per region (inner face, periphery). Frozen patch features may not carry sub-patch double structure at all (AF0 F1 decides that for both targets).

ideas.title: Non-degenerate one-capture negatives: R2b for landmark tools and R2s for diffusion autoencoders
ideas.mechanism: 'Tool on one photo' is the identity for OpenCV (bit-identical in the AR1 smoke test) and a near-exact copy of the photo for DiffAE when its own inverted noise code is used, so R2 hides exactly the processing a morph receives. Build negatives that carry the full single-capture pipeline: R2b = the unchanged landmark tool on (H, H) with the second landmark file re-estimated on the lossless mirror or an integer-shifted copy (two interpolations of one capture, then the tool's own blend); R2s = decode(z_A, slerp(xT_A, fresh Gaussian noise, 0.5)), one photo, the stochastic code refreshed as much as a morph refreshes it. MIPGAN with A = B is already non-degenerate. Audit and train on morph against these negatives, with same-person morphs as the labelled side group.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Every operator that touches a morph's pixels (interpolation, self-averaging, loss of one capture's exact hair and skin detail, decoder steps) also touches the negative. What is left between the classes is a second capture and a second identity, nothing else.
ideas.covers: Landmark and diffusion-autoencoder families (the two where today's R2 is degenerate). GAN: already covered by the A = B optimisation in AG1. Needs a ruling: R2s is a 'processed genuine' image only if one-photo reconstructions are ruled genuine; R2b needs the 'modified path verified against the unchanged tool' allowance.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Diffusion: for the 204 FRLL photos of a43, generate R2s at 20 steps on the GB10 (encode 13 s per image if codes are not cached, decode 1 s; about 50 minutes worst case). Score with the existing A46 d2 CLIP ViT-L/14 probe (trained a43_B vs a43_D, held-out 0.993) and the released MADation ViT-L/14 and ViT-B/16. Prediction: B20 vs R2s AUC at most 0.65, R2s vs D20 at least 0.90, meaning the 0.99 was 'exact copy of a photo versus true render', not identity. Landmark: R2b for the 536 AR1 hosts and both tools (CPU, about 1 minute at the measured 1,841 images per minute), scored by the AR1 scorer next to R2w.
ideas.falsifier: The probe keeps B20 vs R2s AUC at or above 0.85 (then exact-detail fidelity was not the cue and D20 was an adequate negative); and all four releases score R0 vs R2b and R2w vs R2b inside 0.45 to 0.55 (then R2w is enough and R2b adds nothing).
ideas.compute: Under 1 GB10 GPU-hour for R2s; CPU minutes for R2b; scoring in minutes.

Jittered landmark files are a new input to an unchanged tool and must be verified. ideas.title: Spectral crossover map, then one network run at the common Nyquist
ideas.mechanism: History cues (interpolation kernel, JPEG grid, generator high-frequency fingerprint, decoder step count) live above the lowest native sampling limit of any source; identity shrinkage and large-offset ghosts live far below it. First measure, per spatial scale, how readable each is: logistic read-outs on k x k block means of the aligned 512 frame for k from 4 to 64 (numpy features, the form AR3 already uses; no image written). If a band exists where morph evidence is high and history evidence is at chance, train and test the single network only on inputs limited to that band, with a common-support mask (approved constant-colour blanking) to remove border and background.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: By the sampling theorem a cue that exists only above the band is not in the input; freedom from that cue is a property of the input, verified by the history curve sitting at chance, not a hope placed on a loss. The smallest native inter-eye distance I could check is 61 px (corrected MAD22 FaceMorpher median), so an in-frame inter-eye distance near 30 to 35 px is below every checked source's limit.
ideas.covers: Landmark: ghosts with offsets above a few pixels and shape shrinkage survive; fine blend traces do not. GAN and diffusion: only through identity shrinkage. Does not remove low-band cues (colour statistics, expression imbalance, framing; C1 and C3 show they exist), which need masking and balanced cells.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: CPU, about 1 hour, existing frames only. History curves: FRLL native vs existing E7 frames per family; AR1 R0 vs R2w. Morph curves: AR1 R2w vs R4 and R3 vs R4 (both tools), a43 D20 vs B20, h3_sg3 render vs morph. Folds by person. Plot AUC against k and read the crossover.
ideas.falsifier: No scale at which morph AUC exceeds history AUC by at least 0.15 with history AUC at or below 0.60, on the landmark family; or morph AUC at the chosen band below 0.70.
ideas.compute: CPU only for the map. If positive: one LoRA fit per seed (about 1 hour each) on band-limited inputs.
ideas.main_risk: Building band-limited network inputs needs a downscale step, which collides with the rule against new resampling code; only block-mean features or an existing approved path (the E7 function applied uniformly to both classes, or INTER_AREA in ffhq_align) is admissible and needs the author's yes. Accuracy cost on families whose only evidence is fine (AMSL interior). The in-frame inter-eye distance of the 512 frame was not verified.

ideas.title: Virtual morphs in feature space: training pairs with no image pipeline
ideas.mechanism: If a morph's frozen features are close to the midpoint of its contributors' features plus a tool offset, positives need no image generation: average the features of two genuine photos of different persons; negatives are single photos, same-person averages form the side group. Measure linearity first on real morphs with known contributors. Then train a small head on unlimited virtual pairs, adding the measured history offsets (R0 to R1, R0 to R2w, R0 to reconstruction) to both classes at random so the head cannot use them. This is the learned form of idea 1 and removes the 16-to-90-pair limit of the Codex heads.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: There is no pixel pipeline in training, so no pipeline cue can correlate with the label. History directions are injected symmetrically in feature space from existing matched pairs, without any new image code.
ideas.covers: GAN and diffusion latent morphs (generators are built to be semantically linear, so linearity is most plausible there); landmark only if pixel blends are near-linear in the features. Cannot use ghost evidence. Same ceilings as idea 1 for look-alike pairs.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Linearity: on AR1 (536 hosts, contributors in pool.csv), a43 B20 (pairs in the manifest) and GAN32 (P0/P1 with RA/RB), regress centred morph features on centred contributor midpoints in the identity subspace and print R squared and the residual's consistency across pairs. Head: train on virtual pairs from non-AR1 FRGC and colorFERET photos (features only), test on real AR1 R2w vs R4 and R3 vs R4, a43 D20 vs B20, h3_sg3 render vs morph. Minutes once features exist.
ideas.falsifier: Linearity R squared below 0.3 in every backbone; or the virtual-trained head stays below 0.65 on real R2 vs R4 in all three families.
ideas.compute: Features for about 10,000 genuine photos: under 1 GPU-hour; heads: minutes. A LoRA variant (mixing at an intermediate layer) is about 1 hour per fit and only worth running if the frozen version passes.
ideas.main_risk: Averaging any two feature vectors shrinks the norm in every direction, not only identity ones, so a head can learn 'small norm' trivially; same-person averages must be the matched reference for any identity claim. Pixel blends with visible ghosts are off the natural-image manifold and may not be linear in CLIP features. CASIA-WebFace (112 px) is too different from the test frames to add as a source.

Codex frozen heads of 11 Nov with 16 to 90 real pairs (record). One web search this session found no embedding-mixup surrogate for S-MAD (not exhaustive).

ideas.title: Stationarity-cancelling relative features: classify only within-image contrasts of log band energy
ideas.mechanism: Benign channels are spatially stationary: one kernel, one quantiser, one decoder for the whole image, so in log band-energy space they add the same vector at every location. Morphing is not stationary: ghost only where the two faces disagree, sharp at landmark-anchored points and soft between them, blended inside the face hull and untouched outside in splice morphs. Build patch tokens as log energies of a fixed orthonormal filter bank, subtract the per-image mean over tokens for each band, and classify only the remaining deviations with landmark-relative positions. For a linear shift-invariant channel H the term log|H(f)|^2 cancels exactly.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: The invariance is algebraic: a global linear channel changes all tokens of a band by one constant, which the centring removes. This differs from the failed CLIP token normalisation (Astra E2), where the channel effect is not additive in feature space. Leaks from additive noise and JPEG nonlinearity are measured by the E7 shift.
ideas.covers: Landmark, including splice morphs (AMSL, WebMorph: the hardest landmark cells for the best release). Cannot cover GAN or diffusion morphs: a render is stationary. Portrait background blur and face-only retouching are natural non-stationarity and will raise false alarms unless ruled manipulation.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: CPU, about 1 hour, existing frames. 8 x 8 block DCT log energies in 5 radial bands on a 32 x 32 grid of the 512 frame, centred per image, pooled over 6 regions defined by the existing .tem hulls (about 30 numbers). Fit by person folds on AR1 R2w vs R4, test on FRLL-Morphs AMSL, WebMorph, OpenCV, FaceMorpher with native and E7 genuine frames, next to the same features without centring.
ideas.falsifier: E7 rise above 3 EER points with centring; or AUC below 0.70 on both AMSL and WebMorph; or centring removes less than half of the uncentred features' E7 rise.
ideas.compute: CPU only, about 1 hour.
ideas.main_risk: Low absolute power: person-to-person variation of skin versus hair texture is larger than the 3 dB blend effect. A fixed filter bank inside the network may be read as new blur code (it produces no image; needs a ruling). MADMamba's own frequency stream was shown to amplify the sharpness cue (A8, E07), so the centring must be shown to be what matters.

ideas.title: Disagreement-region test for optimisation-based and diffusion morphs: is the same-generator signal in the face or around it?
ideas.mechanism: MIPGAN minimises perceptual and MS-SSIM distance to both source photos as well as an identity loss to both, so where the two photos disagree grossly (hair outline, ears, collar) the optimum is a compromise render, the latent analogue of ghosting. In DiffAE morphs the noise code is a slerp of two maps that each carry one photo's hair and skin detail. Both effects are local and sit where the contributors differ; identity shrinkage is global and sits in the inner face. Probes on inputs with the face blanked or the periphery blanked split the same-generator separation into these two parts, and the ghost-energy head of idea 2 can then be tried zero-shot on renders.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Both classes are renders of one generator at one setting; the only variable is one versus two source photos, and blanking localises where the evidence is. A plain latent average (StyleGAN3 H3) has no structural loss, so the idea predicts a null there, which makes it checkable.
ideas.covers: MIPGAN-type optimisation morphs and DiffAE-based morphs. Not plain latent averaging. An attacker can crop or splice the periphery away, so this is evidence about tools as released, not a guarantee.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: H4b (338 MIPGAN-I-style morphs vs 338 one-host renders of the same generator; bytes alone already give 0.912, so the morphs are smoother somewhere) and a43 (B20 vs C20 and D20). Frozen CLIP-L and DINOv3 probes, 5 folds by person, on three inputs: full frame, periphery blanked, face blanked (approved constant-colour blanking with existing masks). Also PNG bytes of the inner-face crop versus the periphery crop (no GPU). About 30 minutes.
ideas.falsifier: On H4b the face-blanked probe is below 0.60 while the periphery-blanked probe is at or above 0.85: all evidence is inner-face shrinkage, the compromise idea is dead and folds into idea 1. Face-blanked at or above 0.80 supports it.
ideas.compute: About 10 GPU-minutes of feature extraction plus CPU.
ideas.main_risk: H4b's negative is rendered from the same photo as one contributor, so pose and hair match the host and periphery differences may be trivially large. Compromise artefacts in MIPGAN periphery are inferred from the loss, not checked in images. AG1's proper MIPGAN ladder does not exist yet.

MIPGAN, Zhang et al., IEEE T-BIOM 2021, arXiv:2009.01729: loss = 0.0002 perceptual + 10 identity + 1 MS-SSIM + 1 ID-Diff, structural terms against both contributors (checked, ar5iv page opened). Diffusion Autoencoders, arXiv:2111.15640 (checked). Greedy-DiM, Blasingame and Liu, arXiv:2404.06025 (memory; search result seen, page not opened). DDIM-inverted noise is not white Gaussian: pix2pix-zero, arXiv:2302.03027 (memory; search result seen, page not opened).

objections_to_current_plan: The pipeline-matched genuine rung R2 is degenerate in two of three families. OpenCV on one photo is bit-identical to the photo (AR1 smoke test) and a DiffAE reconstruction with its own inverted noise code is a near-exact copy. So 'morph versus pipeline-matched genuine' is in fact 'morph versus untouched photo', and a detector trained on it is free to learn generic interpolation and smoothing, or exact-detail fidelity, which is the same class of cue as the E7 failure. R2w (added today) restores the warp but not the tool's self-blend, and nothing restores the diffusion case.

The 'reads morphing' rule requires an R0 to R2 share of at most 0.2. On landmark builds that share is zero by construction, so the rule can be passed by a detector that reads warp and blend traces. The rule should be stated on a non-degenerate one-capture negative (R2w or R2b, and R2s for diffusion).

Spread-matched renders (X4) are used as a verdict-bearing R2 in AG5. A single-identity render pulled toward the mean code is identity-diluted, in effect a morph with the mean face. Using it as the genuine class removes the only signal an ideal latent morph leaves and pre-decides a null. CONCLUSIONS (l.20, l.163) already says a matched render is 'almost the same kind of image by construction'; the audit table should not print 'reads the benchmark' on that arm.

File-size floors are applied to same-generator, same-size, lossless comparisons (H4b 0.912, H1 0.62 to 0.68). There, PNG bytes measure the texture energy that morphing removes, so they are a mediator of the morph effect, not a construction cue. 'Not above the bytes floor' does not show absence of a morph signal. The right control for smoothness is a blur-matched one-capture negative, because absolute smoothness cannot be told from benign blur.

The twin contrast cannot work for same-person latent mixes even in principle: decode(mix(w_A, w_A')) is another valid render of the same person, and its identity part is unchanged. The author counts these as morphs, so the plan carries a guaranteed miss that should be written as a stated limit, not tested as a hypothesis with a pass rule.

Image-level labels allow any image-constant cue, whatever the loss. AF0's dense target is the right direction, but its alpha target is unidentifiable where the two layers agree and teaches 'locally smooth means mixed', which turns benign blur into a false alarm on a processed genuine photo, the error the author ruled out.

The plan's generator half needs 35 to 150 GPU-hours of twin generation before the first decisive number, and the author objected twice to generation time. The identity-shrinkage test and virtual feature-space morphs need no generation and can fail or pass tonight.

The most promising positive number in the record is being read as a negative: the A46 d2 CLIP ViT-L/14 probe separates our diffusion morphs from reconstructions at 0.993 held-out and published DiM families at 0.81 to 0.95, with the E7 control at 0.48. It was filed as 'not readable' because one control's bound exceeded 0.60. Nobody has asked what it reads. My lens says: loss of one capture's exact detail (x_T mixing), which a one-photo refreshed decode would share. That is one hour of work and decides the diffusion method half.

R3m (a photo morphed with its own mirror image) is listed as a one-person rung. In identity and lighting terms the mirror is a different face (asymmetry and light direction flip), so it should behave like a look-alike morph; by the ruling it is on the morph side. It should not be read as a pipeline-only or twin negative.

The R3 versus R4 guard G1 matches only landmark distance. Two sessions of one person and two different people also differ in hair, collar and lighting mismatch, which drive ghost energy in the periphery; without a periphery-blanked read the side study can be decided by hair, not identity.

physics.detectability_analysis:
LANDMARK MORPHS, I = (1-a)*W_A(A) + a*W_B(B) inside the face hull, optionally spliced into A. (L1) Interpolation from the piecewise-affine warp: exists, but any later resize above about 1.5x or print-scan removes it, and a global resize of a genuine photo leaves the same trace with one map; only its variation between triangles is tool-specific. (L2) Texture averaging: detail that is uncorrelated between the layers keeps (1-a)^2 + a^2 of its variance, 0.5 at a = 0.5 (minus 3 dB), 0.82 at a = 0.1; sensor noise likewise. Real, but a blur, a denoiser or a shrink-and-enlarge cycle does the same or more (E7 took Laplacian variance from 175 to 16 on one pool). In absolute form it is indistinguishable from benign processing; this is the cue the record shows detectors following. (L3) Superposition: structures present in one layer appear at weight a, displaced structures appear twice. Resize and compression do not create it. It survives a channel only where the displacement exceeds the channel's blur width: periphery (hair outline, ears, collar, tens of pixels) survives everything including print-scan; inner-face marks (moles, wrinkles, brow hairs, 0 to 3 px at 512) merge into 'slightly soft' and are lost at passport sizes. Splice tools remove the periphery evidence by design, which is why AMSL is the hard cell (14.7 percent for the best release). (L4) Inside versus outside inconsistency in splice morphs: ratios cancel global channels; portrait background blur and face-only retouching mimic it. (L5) Shrinkage: landmark coordinates are averaged exactly, identity variance scales by (1+c)/2; survives every benign channel; bounded. Same-person morphs carry L1 to L3 (two sessions differ in hair and collar) but no identity shrinkage. Not detectable: a near 0, look-alikes with c near 1, and after print-scan a splice morph of look-alikes leaves only L5.

GAN LATENT MORPHS, x = G(w_m), w_m the mean of two inverted codes or an optimised point near it (MIPGAN). (G1) Generator fingerprint and inversion loss: identical in a one-identity render, not morph-specific, gone after print-scan; legitimate only if reconstructions are ruled manipulated. (G2) Latent shrinkage: Cov(w_m) = (1+c)/2 times the single-code covariance. In the generator's own latent this is huge (squared norm over 512 dimensions: mean 512, SD 32 against mean 256, SD 16 at c = 0, about 10 SD), which is why spread alone labels H3 perfectly (A39) and frozen probes reach 0.91 (A38). Most of those dimensions are pose, light, hair and background, which a same-person mix also shrinks; the morph-specific part is the identity subspace only. (G3) MIPGAN only: structural losses to both photos give compromise rendering where the photos disagree (inferred from the loss, not verified in images). Not detectable: with an ideal generator G(w_m) is a valid image of a plausible third person and no pixel statistic separates it from G(w_C). The best possible single-image test is the density ratio between midpoint and single-code distributions, that is identity shrinkage, with AUC about Phi(sqrt(d/2)*(1-s)/sqrt(1+s^2)), s = ((1+c)/2+n)/(1+n). Examples: d = 30, c = 0.3, n = 0.5 gives 0.76; d = 100 gives 0.90; d = 30, c = 0.6 gives 0.65; d = 10, c = 0.3 gives 0.66. A same-person latent mix against another render of that person is not detectable in principle except as 'too neutral'.

DIFFUSION-AUTOENCODER MORPHS, x = Dec(lerp(z_A, z_B), slerp(xT_A, xT_B)) with N DDIM steps (MorDIFF, DiM; Greedy-DiM adds an identity-guided search). (D1) Decoder trace, step count, 256 px native size: shared by every decode, not specific (A43 shows a release following step count). (D2) Exact-detail fidelity: Dec(z_A, xT_A) reproduces the photo almost exactly; a decode with a mixed or refreshed noise code carries no single capture's hair and skin detail. This separates morphs from plain reconstructions strongly (CLIP-L probe 0.993, A46 d2) but is a property of refreshing x_T, not of a second identity; it lives in fine detail and dies under a channel. (D3) Semantic shrinkage: z_sem is 512-d and normalised to zero mean and unit variance; lerp shrinks the centred squared norm by (1+c)/2; re-encoding with the public encoder should recover it (not verified). This is the morph-specific signal. (D4) Greedy-DiM's identity guidance toward one FR model: no single-image test known. Not detectable: as for GAN.

ACROSS FAMILIES. Only two kinds of evidence are both specific to morphing and robust to a benign channel applied to both classes: superposition at offsets larger than the channel's blur (landmark tools only) and identity shrinkage (all families, bounded by pair similarity and by how well identity can be estimated from one image). Everything else is either processing history, which a processed genuine photo shares, or renderer evidence, which a one-identity render shares.
physics.sota_definition:
State of the art, operationally: one network, one threshold fixed on genuine photos of the training pools (never on FRLL), five seeds reported as mean with person-clustered 95 percent intervals. On each landmark cell of FRLL-Morphs and corrected MAD22, with the genuine class in its E7 form (R1 vs R4), EER and APCER at BPCER 5 percent are at least non-inferior (within 2 points) to the best released detector scored under the same condition (MADation ViT-L/14: 1.0 / 1.0 / 14.7 / 4.4 on FRLL), and better on at least the splice cells. On GAN and diffusion cells the claim is made on the one-capture-negative contrast (non-degenerate R2 vs R4), where every released detector is at 0.40 to 0.49 today, so the first lower bound above 0.65 is state of the art; the native benchmark number is printed as a descriptive column only.

Shortcut-free, operationally, is five checks on the same network: (1) history null: genuine R0 vs R1 AUC inside 0.45 to 0.55 and mean shift at most 0.3 SD, on FRLL and on one pool never trained on; (2) one-capture pipeline null: R0 vs non-degenerate R2 (R2w or R2b; R2s for DiffAE; A = B for MIPGAN) AUC at most 0.60, and BPCER on R1 and R2 at the operating threshold within 2 points of BPCER on R0 (for generators this check applies only if reconstructions are ruled processed genuine); (3) the detector beats the best non-content baseline (file attributes, border, background, colour statistics, expression) with a paired lower bound above zero; (4) dose: score rises monotonically with mixing fraction and falls with contributor similarity; (5) ceiling: the achieved AUC on latent morphs is printed next to the ceiling predicted from genuine-only identity statistics, and no detection of same-person latent mixes is claimed. A detector that passes (2) cannot also lead the native GAN and diffusion benchmark columns, because the competitors' numbers there contain the render and history cue; the paper has to say this in one sentence.

ideas.title: HalfTwin: train each landmark morph against its own two unblended warped halves
ideas.mechanism: A landmark morph is 0.5*warp(H to M) + 0.5*warp(B to M), with M the mid shape. Store the two warped halves W_H and W_B (one capture each, same warp field, same landmark geometry M, same hull mask, border, canvas and storage as the morph) and use them as the genuine class; the morph is their pixel mean. Positives at other mixing fractions (0.1 to 0.5) and same-person positives (H with a second session S) are composed from stored halves, so dose targets are free. Loss: image label, a within-triple ranking term (morph above both of its halves) and a mixing-fraction regression. FaceMorpher's own calls also give a 2 x 2 of face (single or blended) by background (single or blended), so the label can be tied to the face and not to the background ghost; in the approved h1_build.py the half is the `host` image the script already computes before Poisson cloning.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Morph and negatives come from the same two photos through the same calls, so source, person, session, expression, pose, colour, background, crop, border fraction, landmark geometry (kills the eye-geometry and shape-averageness cues), warp resampling and file storage are identical or exactly averaged between classes. The only thing the morph has that its halves lack is the superposition of two captures. Every person is in both classes with the same image content, so memorising identities or photos cannot help. Pair lists are round-robin (each person host and donor equally often, 5 to 10 donors per host drawn from look-alike and landmark-distance bins that overlap the same-person bins), batches hold whole triples, splits are by person with both contributors in one split. The one legitimate cue that blur could mimic (loss of fine detail from averaging) is handled by ideas 3 and 5.
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes, all Delaunay tools including splice and Poisson variants (OpenCV engine, FaceMorpher, h1_build). GAN: no. Diffusion: no (there is no pixel superposition to isolate).

Head B: halves vs morph. Read (1) AUC of head B, halves vs morph, held-out tool; (2) share of halves flagged by head A at its EER threshold; (3) both heads on existing FRLL frames native and E7 and on /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/mad22_canonical_E7_inputs_v3_20261109T113746Z/{native,e7}; (4) unseen source: /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/h1_poisson morphs against the warped host from the same approved script (598 pairs, CASIA).

ideas.title: SMDD-T: rebuild the SMDD attack class with balanced partners and halves (SMDD-only protocol)
ideas.mechanism: Fact found this session: in the SMDD release on disk all 15,000 training morphs share only five second contributors (img054553 3,444 morphs; img282038 3,310; img496816 3,260; img337488 2,813; img099545 2,173), and no bona fide render is ever a contributor. Rebuild the attack class from SMDD's own renders with the unchanged OpenCV engine at 256 px: 15,000 pairs in which every render is partner at most twice (round-robin over the cached look-alike table). Add the two warped halves of each pair as genuine images, so every synthetic identity appears under both labels. All files are 256 x 256 PNG from one tool run (the release has about 6% off-size morphs). Four arms separate the changes: release as is; our tool on the release pair list; balanced partners; balanced partners plus halves.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Removes three SMDD-side cues at once: five recurring partner faces and their ghosted backgrounds in every positive, disjoint identity pools for the two classes, and off-size morph files. Halves give the genuine class the warp. No real person is used, so the field's SMDD-only protocol and its privacy argument are kept; SelfMAD is the precedent for building attacks from SMDD renders. 25,000 identities make memorising genuine faces useless.

ideas.title: Region-partial morphs with patch-level mixing targets: each image is its own control
ideas.mechanism: From stored halves compose P = W_H + m * a * (W_B - W_H), where m is a hard mask over a random subset of landmark-defined regions (eyes and brows, nose, mouth, cheeks, forehead; 20 to 80% of the hull) and a is 0.3 to 0.5. The target is the 16 x 16 (or 24 x 24 at 336 px) map of second-capture weight; a per-token head on the patch tokens of the same backbone predicts it and the image score is the mean of the top fifth of face tokens. Full morphs (m = 1) and halves (m = 0) stay in the mix. Decoy seams (the same region filled from a second, slightly different warp of the same capture) carry target 0 so that a region boundary alone is not a positive.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Inside one image every global property is constant (source, history, file, identity, pose, expression, colour, border), yet the target varies over space and its location is randomised independently of content. No image-level cue, known or unknown, can predict it. It also gives 256 targets per image instead of 1, which matters with 536 hosts, and it yields localisation maps for the paper.
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes. GAN: no (no spatially local mixing). Diffusion: no clean version (noise maps can be mixed locally but the semantic code is global).
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Same AR1 halves as idea 1; partial positives composed in memory (array arithmetic and polygon masks, nothing resampled). Frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 patch tokens, per-token logistic head, 5-fold by person, train on one tool and test on the other. Read interior-token AUC (boundary tokens ignored), image-level AUC on full morphs vs halves when trained on partial images only, and the decoy flag rate. Compare with idea 1's image-level head.
ideas.falsifier: Dead if interior-token AUC on the held-out tool is below 0.70, or if image-level transfer to full morphs is more than 0.05 AUC below idea 1's head, or if decoy seams are flagged at more than half the rate of true partial regions (then it reads seams).
ideas.compute: CPU composition on the fly; token features about 5 GB for 5,000 images; about 15 GPU-min; heads minutes. LoRA version about 1 GPU-h per seed.
ideas.main_risk: Hard mask edges create seams that full-face benchmark morphs do not have; the transfer test decides. ideas.title: History crossed at the source: the tool run on already-shrunk copies and on pools of different native size
ideas.mechanism: Give both classes every history by applying history before the tool, never after it. (a) The 25,000 registered shrunk-and-enlarged SMDD renders already on disk are run through the unchanged tool: morphs and halves from shrunk sources, from native sources, and mixed (one native, one shrunk), giving a 2 x 2 of history by label. (b) The unchanged tools are run at the native sizes of the pools: 256 px SMDD, 512 px FRGC/colorFERET frames, 1,024 px FFHQ (68_hires_morph.py already does this). (c) A sampler knob sets the training correlation between history and label to +1, 0 or -1, to draw a reliance curve; the reported model uses 0.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: History is independent of the label by construction and the blend trace always sits on top of the history, so it is never degraded. That is the difference from the class-symmetric augmentation that cost accuracy in A47 I-1, where both classes were degraded after morphing. No new blur, resize or compression code: only existing registered outputs, the unchanged tools and the model's own input resize.
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes. GAN and diffusion: only the genuine side (it removes the photo-history cue that carries the diffusion cells), so native diffusion numbers are expected to fall.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Shrunk copies: /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a47/data47/i3/train/smdd_a47e7/os25k_bf_t (25,000, same names as the originals, so the cached landmarks apply if the canvas is unchanged). Build 5,000 pairs x {native, shrunk, mixed} morphs and halves on CPU. Frozen CLIP-L heads: halves-only native (idea 2, arm 4) against the history-crossed version. Read the flag rate on FRLL E7 photos at the threshold that flags 5% of native FRLL photos, and landmark-cell EER native and E7, on existing frames.
ideas.falsifier: Fails if the gap between E7 and native flag rates is not at least halved relative to the native-only arm, or if native landmark-cell mean EER worsens by more than 3 points.
ideas.compute: CPU 15 min; features 5 GPU-min; heads minutes.
ideas.main_risk: One dose and one kernel (the registered 3.2x shrink) is a single history; it may not generalise to JPEG or other kernels. Extending it needs the author's yes to run the registered degrade call on new inputs. Low novelty on its own; it is a hygiene axis for ideas 1 and 2.

ideas.title: Code-crossed latent mixes: thousands of generator pairs by decode-only reuse of cached encodings
ideas.mechanism: Encoding is the expensive step (13 s per image) and is already paid: 434 DiffAE code files (512-d semantic code plus 3 x 256 x 256 noise map) for about 204 FERET/FRGC persons with two captures each, and 128 StyleGAN3 w+ codes seen on disk (256 per the inventory). Decode new two-person mixes for a round-robin list across blocks (each person in about 10 pairs) at 20 steps, about 1 s each. For a subset decode the 2 x 2: semantic code own or mixed, by noise map own or mixed, plus a one-identity render whose semantic code is shrunk toward the mean to match the mix (the spread control that does not yet exist for DiffAE). Train with two targets, identity mixing and noise-map mixing, on person-disjoint dyadic splits.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: All classes are outputs of one decoder at one step count, size and storage, from the same captures. Crossing the two codes separates identity mixing from the interpolation trace of the noise map, and the spread control separates it from nearness to the mean face. Every person appears in reconstructions and in many mixes. It replaces the underpowered 16 to 90 pair tests with about 2,000 pairs without new inversion.
ideas.covers: Diffusion: yes for the DiffAE family (MorDIFF, DiM use it). GAN: StyleGAN3 latent-mean morphs, with coarse layers by fine layers as the 2 x 2; not MIPGAN. Landmark: no.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Codes: /mnt/t7/smad_research/diffae-expanded123-v1/run/<block>/{a0,a1,b0,b1}-latent.npz; negatives already rendered there (RA0, RA1, RB0, RB1; 408). Not identity if (mixed semantic code, own noise) vs reconstruction is below 0.55 while (own semantic code, mixed noise) vs reconstruction is above 0.70, or if the spread control brings the main AUC under 0.55.

ideas.title: Aligned photo and re-render pairs as a second output of the same network (needs the reconstruction ruling)
ideas.mechanism: Add a second sigmoid output, 're-rendered by a generator', trained only on pairs of a photo and its own one-identity reconstruction stored in one identical form (the photo is the generator's exact input, the render its output). The first output stays 'two captures combined'. If reconstructions are ruled manipulated, the benchmark-comparable score is a fixed noisy-OR of the two outputs; if they are ruled genuine, the second output is reported as a separate flag and excluded from the morph score. One network either way.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Within a pair, content, identity, pose, crop, pixel size and storage are identical; only the encode and decode pass differs, the B-Free and DDA recipe. E7 photos and R2* images go in as re-rendered = 0 so softness cannot stand in for rendering. It turns what the audit calls a shortcut (generator output vs camera) into a labelled, history-matched target, and it keeps the blend output clean of it.
ideas.covers: GAN and diffusion: yes, as 'rendered', which is the only route I see to competitive numbers on MIPGAN, MorDIFF and DiM cells that survives history matching, and only if ruled legitimate. Landmark: handled by the first output.

objections_to_current_plan: The pipeline-matched genuine rung is empty for landmark tools. AR1's own prereg records that OpenCV tool(H, H) is bit-identical to H and FaceMorpher differs by at most 1 grey level in 14% of pixels. Training on R2 vs R4 is therefore photo vs morph from the same frames: only the morph class carries warp resampling, averaging softness, hull mask and background ghost. Nothing tells the network that resampling or softness alone is not a morph, which is how SelfMAD fails under E7.
After the author's ruling, same-person morphs are positives, so the plan has no hard negative left for landmark morphs. It kept the twin vocabulary but lost its negative class.

SMDD, the protocol reference, has a construction defect that is not in the record. In the release on disk all 15,000 training morphs share five second contributors (img054553 3,444; img282038 3,310; img496816 3,260; img337488 2,813; img099545 2,173; counted from file names in /mnt/t7/Datasety/downloads/SMDD/SMDD_release_train/m15k_t and confirmed by eye on three morphs); the evaluation split uses five others; and 0 of the 3,858 contributors are in the bona fide folder (they are in os25k_m_t). Every SMDD-trained row may partly detect five faces and their backgrounds. The paper text describes 5 random partners per key image.

No history variation exists in the planned training set (one 512 px PNG history; R1 exists only as E7 outputs on FRLL test persons). Invariance to photo history is hoped for, not trained and not testable on the training pools.

Too few identities for LoRA: 536 hosts, and each negative is literally one photo seen every epoch. The main contrast (one capture vs two captures) needs no second photo per person, so 50,000 SMDD renders and 70,000 FFHQ persons are unused.
No SMDD-only arm with matched negatives. If the method trains on FRGC and colorFERET, reviewers will credit real data and the comparison with MADation and SelfMAD is not like for like.

Generator families: the plan treats a one-photo reconstruction as genuine although that is not ruled, and under that reading AD1 (R2 vs R4 0.40 to 0.49) and AG5 (maximum 0.61 over 55 networks) predict chance. Spending about 150 GPU-h on 10,000-pair generator sets before a 2,000-pair gate is not justified; the gate can be built in under 2 GPU-h by decoding new mixes from cached codes.

The base-model argument is weaker than stated. The MADation ViT-L/14 release does not move under E7 in EER, but AD1 shows that at its MorDIFF threshold it flags 51% of E7 photos and 82% of reconstructions, and its R2 vs R4 is 0.486.
Image-level labels waste what the build knows (mask and mixing fraction per pixel). Dense targets and graded positives are free once halves are stored.

FRLL twins mix a neutral and a smiling photo; AD1 shows the R3 to R4 step is partly an expression effect, and C1 shows 11 of 17 benchmark cells have neutral-only morphs against a half-smiling genuine class. Training sets must cross expression with label; sets built from halves do so automatically.

The final test on FRLL persons x held-out tool has about 100 persons (interval about plus or minus 0.08), so most cells will read mixed. The CASIA H1 set can be a second, unseen-source twin test without any second photo, because the approved h1_build.morph already computes the warped host.

data.sota_definition: Target that my training sets assume. Positive: pixels or codes of two different captures were combined (two persons; two photos of one person as a labelled side group). Negative: one capture, whatever was done to it (crop, alignment, tool warp, resize, compression, and generator reconstruction if so ruled). State of the art, operationally: one network, five seeds, last checkpoint, and (1) on history-matched benchmark cells (FRLL and corrected MAD22 morphs against E7 photos) EER no worse than the released MADation ViT-L/14 (FRLL landmark 1.0 / 1.0 / 14.7 / 4.4, Greedy-DiM 9.8) with a paired interval; (2) on the main ladder contrast (one-capture tool output against two-capture morph; held-out tool, unseen persons, unseen source) AUC at least 0.90 with lower bound above 0.85. Shortcut-free, operationally: at the threshold giving 10% missed morphs, the false-alarm rate on every one-capture rung (camera photo, E7 photo, R2* one-photo tool run, warp-only half) is within 5 points of the camera-photo rate; the best non-content baseline (file attributes, border mask, background thumbnail) is beaten with a paired lower bound above 0; the score rises monotonically with mixing fraction. If reconstructions are ruled genuine, the same rule covers reconstructions, and then I expect no detector, ours included, to be state of the art on GAN and diffusion cells; the paper should say so with the measured limit.
data.detectability_analysis: Landmark (pixel blend). Detectable and legitimate: superposition of two captures. In a 50/50 blend, detail that is uncorrelated between the sources keeps 0.71 of its amplitude (0.76 at 30/70, 0.91 at 10/90) while shared coarse structure is kept, and misregistered edges double (iris, lids, nostrils, lip line, brows, hairline). Not legitimate alone, because one photo can show them: warp resampling (identical in the warp-only half), softening (a one-photo tool run with landmark sets 1 px apart attenuates the 0.25 cycles/px band by the same 0.71), hull or splice seam, border. Background ghost outside the face is real but tool-specific and absent in splice morphs such as AMSL. Identity typicality: norm shrink sqrt((1+c)/2) is 0.79 for the AR1 two-person pairs (median cosine 0.23) and 0.97 for same-person pairs (0.87), so same-person morphs carry almost no typicality signal; their ghost offsets are small (not measured), which predicts they are detectable only at 336 px or more. Shape averageness is present in both classes of my sets by construction, so it is unused. GAN (latent mean, MIPGAN). Detectable: that the image was rendered by a generator (0.90 to 0.95 against camera photos for existing features), legitimate only if reconstructions are ruled manipulated and only against history-matched photos; latent averageness (frozen probes 0.91, gone under spread matching, 0.42 to 0.52). Not detectable on current evidence: a second identity as such (maximum 0.61 over 55 networks, on a set where only 48% of morphs verify against both contributors). MIPGAN optimisation traces: unknown until AG1. Diffusion (DiffAE family). Detectable: rendering and its settings (step count) and storage size. Unknown at adequate power: mixing of the semantic code (identity) versus mixing of the noise map (a processing trace); zero-shot R2 vs R4 is 0.40 to 0.49 for three releases and trained heads exist only at 16 to 90 pairs. Idea 6 separates the two; my expectation is that semantic mixing alone is near chance beyond typicality.

ideas.title: Identity dose inside the morph class: contributor-distance slope as an audit tonight, then as a training target
ideas.mechanism: Inside one morph family every image shares tool, file format, size and history; only the pair of contributors changes. So the response of a score to the face-recognition distance between the two contributors (delta = 1 minus cosine of the two source photos) cannot be produced by benchmark construction. First read this slope for the released detectors from score files that already exist, family by family. Then train a head output on delta with a loss that compares morphs only with morphs of the same tool (rank loss within the batch), one-photo images anchored at 0; the predicted delta is the detection score.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Neutralised by construction: every cue that separates the two classes of a benchmark cell (container, pixel size, bytes, JPEG history, resampling history of the genuine photos, renderer versus camera, border, colour canvas), because the genuine class does not enter and these properties are constant inside the morph class. In training the partner is assigned by a permutation that is independent of tool and source, so no pipeline property carries information about delta. Not neutralised: things that grow with dissimilarity without being identity (warp size, cross-sex or skin-tone pairs, expression pair, so stratify neutral and smiling), pre-selection of look-alike pairs by benchmark authors (it shrinks the range of delta), and the level of the score on genuine photos at test. Needs no ruling.
ideas.covers: Audit: landmark, GAN and diffusion (FRLL-Morphs 5 families, MorDIFF, DiM 6 families; MAD22 only on the old 185 + 4,069 subset, descriptive). Training: landmark now (AR1 pool: 536 pairs, median cosine host to partner 0.23, host to own second photo 0.87, plus 300 graded hosts); DiffAE (A43, expanded123) and StyleGAN3 (GAN32) only at small size. Cannot cover look-alike pairs, and says nothing about false alarms on genuine photos.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Zero GPU, about 30 to 45 minutes. For the four releases (and the M3, M3L seeds) read /home/narolski/mambamorph-code/smadcvpr_runs/A12_scored/A12REL/<release>/scores_eval.npz, parse the contributor pair from each morph file name, take delta from the FRLL photo embeddings (/mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/frll_src_emb.npz), and compute Spearman(score, delta) per family with a person bootstrap, split by expression. Positive control: the face-recognition oracle (lower of the morph's two cosines to its contributors) must show a slope of at least 0.3 in absolute value, else the family has no power. Stress test with a deliberate confound: on AR1 train the delta head with high-delta pairs taken only from OpenCV and low-delta pairs only from FaceMorpher; a pooled regression must lose its slope when the tools are swapped at test, the within-tool rank loss must keep it.
ideas.falsifier: Audit: with oracle power shown, rho at most 0.10 with upper bound below 0.20 for the MADation ViT-L/14 release and for M3L on all four FRLL landmark families means even the rows that hold under E7 do not read identity distance. Training: within-class Spearman on held-out persons and the left-out tool with lower bound at or below 0, or a slope drop above 0.05 under the tool swap, kills the idea.
ideas.compute: Audit: CPU only, under 1 hour. Training variant: minutes on cached frozen features (AR1 features are about 10 GPU-minutes on the DGX).
ideas.main_risk: Restricted range of delta in the benchmarks if pairs were chosen as look-alikes (not verified), so a flat slope may be lack of power; the oracle check is there for that. For landmark morphs the slope may run through ghost strength and warp size, which are consequences of two identities but also of pose.

ideas.title: Non-degenerate one-photo rungs and partner-independent geometry for the landmark ladder
ideas.mechanism: The landmark rung R2 is empty today: the AR1 pre-registration records that OpenCV run on one photo returns the photo bit for bit and FaceMorpher differs by at most 1 grey level in about 14 % of pixels. Add R2w: the unchanged tool run on a photo and on a copy of the same photo shifted by an odd number of whole pixels (array slicing, landmarks shifted with it), which forces real half-pixel warps and an average of two resampled copies of one capture, perfectly registered. Optional harder rung R2g: the unchanged tool run on the same photo twice, the second time with the landmark file of the person's other session, which gives a one-photo image with the twin's warp fields and a self-ghost. For the twin contrast, make warp size independent of the label: pick each partner B so that its landmark distance to the host falls in the same bin as the host's distance to its own second photo, or build all rungs at a geometry that does not depend on the partner with a warp path verified bit-exact against the tool. Train and judge on R2w (genuine) against R3 and R4.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Neutralised by construction: interpolation smoothing, number of warps, tool arithmetic and storage path (all present in R2w with a single capture); warp magnitude (matched or crossed, so a geometry-only classifier is at 0.5 by design); properties of the partner photo (the same set of photos serves as second photo and as partner in AR1). Not neutralised: the second capture (independent noise and fine texture averaged), which is the intended signal under the ruling that same-person morphs are morphs; the second identity; history added after the tool (benchmark resize and JPEG). Needs a ruling that a one-photo tool output with a real warp is a processed genuine image; R2g needs its own ruling; no ruling on reconstructions needed.
ideas.covers: Landmark only. Not GAN or diffusion, whose one-photo rung (the reconstruction) is already non-trivial.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Zero GPU, 10 minutes: geometry-only classifier R3 versus R4 on the 536 AR1 hosts from landmark distances in the .tem files (the Codex transcript of 10 Nov reports 0.81 pooled and 0.92 on FERET for rendering geometry on its 64-block panel). CPU 10 minutes: build R2w (and R2g) for 536 FRGC and colorFERET hosts and the 102 FRLL hosts with both unchanged tools (the tools take the landmark file as a separate argument). About 20 GPU-minutes: score the four releases and a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 probe; report AUC R0 versus R2w, R2w versus R3, R2w versus R4. Stress test with a deliberately confounded training set: one probe trained on R0 versus R4 (confounded with tool processing, as benchmarks are) and one on R2w versus R4; test both on R0 versus R2w.
ideas.falsifier: Geometry-only AUC at or below 0.60 and every detector's R0 versus R2w AUC inside 0.45 to 0.55: nothing to fix, drop the idea. Conversely, if the probe trained on R2w reaches less than 0.75 on R2w versus R4 for FRLL persons while R0 versus R4 is 0.90 or more, landmark detection in these features was tool processing, which is a headline number against the method half.
ideas.compute: CPU 10 to 15 minutes for the builds; 20 to 30 GPU-minutes on the DGX for scoring and features.
ideas.main_risk: A half-pixel shift is one kind of processing only, and the shift size and the realism of R2g are choices that must be fixed before scoring. Geometry matching reduces the pool (1,399 candidate subjects in the AR1 summary, so it should be feasible; not verified).
