ideas.title: Matched-set conditional likelihood with a planted-confound flip test
ideas.mechanism: Treat every host as a matched set: its one-photo rungs, same-person morph, two-person morph and graded mixings, per tool or generator. Train only with a within-set likelihood (softmax over the set for which image is the morph, or ordered pairs), never comparing images of different sets. Fit the operating threshold afterwards on processed genuine images of validation persons only. Report for every trained model the flip gap: AUC on a test set where a planted cue agrees with the label minus AUC where it is reversed.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Exact in the weak sense: any cue that is constant within a set (host photo, background, source set, tool, storage, session) has no within-set contrast, and class imbalance between sets, tools, sources or families cannot be exploited. This is the matched case-control argument. Image-level cross-entropy has no such property, and the planned pool is unbalanced (same-person morphs exist only for multi-session sources, graded sets add positives for 300 hosts, generator panels have 64 to 102 blocks against 536 landmark hosts). Not neutralised: cues that differ inside a set (handled by the previous and next ideas) and the level of the score across sets at test. For GAN and diffusion sets the open ruling on reconstructions decides whether the reconstruction sits on the genuine side of the set.
ideas.covers: All three families wherever matched sets exist: landmark (AR1), StyleGAN3 (GAN32, 64 plus 32 blocks), DiffAE (expanded123, 102 blocks), MIPGAN once AG1 has run.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 and DINOv3 ViT-L/16 features of the AR1 images under /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img (about 10,000 images, about 10 GPU-minutes), linear heads, folds that hold out both persons of every morph, final test on the 102 FRLL hosts. Arms: cross-entropy versus conditional likelihood. Planted confounds: (i) a grey corner square (constant-colour blanking) on all images of half the hosts, with those hosts sampled at 9 morphs per genuine image and the others at 1 per 9; (ii) natural: OpenCV sets morph-heavy, FaceMorpher sets genuine-heavy. Score same-sign and reversed test sets.
ideas.falsifier: Conditional arm flip gap above 0.03 with an interval excluding 0, or clean-set AUC more than 0.03 below cross-entropy. If the cross-entropy flip gap is below 0.05 the stress was too weak; repeat at 19 to 1 before any conclusion.
ideas.compute: Minutes once features exist.
ideas.main_risk: It is an incremental change (a ranking term was already suggested as an add-on in the method notes) and it gives no invariance of the score at test; its value is to make pooled multi-family training safe and to supply the stress figure.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Conditional logistic regression for matched case-control studies (Breslow and Day, memory). CoRe, conditional variance penalty with grouping by identity, arXiv:1710.11469 (checked via search). MatchDG, arXiv:2006.07500 (checked via search). Group DRO, arXiv:1911.08731 (memory). Codex joint GAN plus DiffAE group-robust heads, no stable gain on 16 plus 74 pairs (record).

ideas.title: Split-face randomised blending: the ladder inside one image, with patch-level targets
ideas.mechanism: For each host build composites in which every region of the face (Delaunay triangles, or a coarse grid) is randomly given one of three treatments with equal area: host only, half host plus half the host's other-session photo, half host plus half another person. One file, one history, one host. A head on patch tokens predicts the treatment of each token, and the loss is computed after subtracting the image's mean logit (or as a ranking between tokens of the same image), so nothing that is constant over the image can lower it. At test the image score is the mean token logit over the face, with the level set on genuine images; the same composites give an area-dose audit for released image-level detectors and a map of which facial regions carry identity evidence. This also gives the paper's original pixel-wise head real within-image targets.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Treatment is randomised within the image, so every cue that is a function of the file, tool run, host, storage, resolution, compression, colour pipeline, source set or expression has exactly zero mutual information with the token label; the centred loss removes even the finite-sample incentive when balance is broken. Not neutralised: local consequences of the partner (blur, ghost offsets, partner warp size), which are the intended signal or identity-linked; the seam between regions (symmetric: it shows where, not which side); and the absolute level of the score under a new history at test. Needs permission for a pixel-selection composite of two unchanged tool outputs, and for a shared-geometry three-source blend verified bit-exact against the tool with an all-partner mask; no ruling on reconstructions.
ideas.covers: Landmark by construction. GAN and diffusion cannot be built this way (global latent codes) and are expected to fail as a transfer test, because latent morphs have no local double structure.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Tonight's version needs no warp change: select blocks between the existing R3 and R4 PNGs (and R2) of the same host and tool in /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img/frgcferet, 536 hosts by 2 tools by 4 random masks, seam tokens excluded. Frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 and CLIP ViT-L/14 at 336 patch tokens, logistic token head, both persons held out. Read: (a) within-image token AUC, two-person region versus same-person region and blended versus host-only, on the left-out tool; (b) transfer to whole images: mean-token score on R2, R3, R4 of the FRLL pool; (c) score shift on the 204 FRLL photos under the existing variants jpeg50, resample50, blur1, resmatch (paths in /mnt/t7/smad_research/astra-e2-v2/INPUTS.json). Stress test: plant a grey corner square on images whose morphed area is 75 % and none on images with 25 %; compare a plain token cross-entropy head with the centred loss on the reversed test set.
ideas.falsifier: Held-out token AUC below 0.60 for two-person versus same-person regions means no local identity evidence in these features; below 0.75 for blended versus host-only kills it for blending too. Token AUC high but whole-image R2 versus R4 below 0.75 on FRLL persons means the local evidence does not aggregate. Centred-loss flip gap above 0.03 means the guarantee is not realised.
ideas.compute: CPU 10 minutes for composites; about 10 GPU-minutes for tokens of about 9,000 images on two backbones; heads in minutes. A LoRA version is about 1 hour per seed.
ideas.main_risk: The token evidence may be mostly blur level, so a resampled genuine photo is flagged everywhere (no test-time guarantee); adding one-photo warp regions as a fourth, genuine treatment addresses this. Patch size of 14 to 16 pixels may be too coarse for ghost detail (not verified).
ideas.closest_prior_work: Seibold, Hilsmann, Eisert: partial morphs with artefacts only in predefined areas (Feature Focus, Computers 2021; JISA 2020, arXiv:1806.04265; checked via search snippets, full text not opened; no same-person control region, not used for shortcut immunity). Face X-ray, arXiv:1912.13458 (checked via search). Pair-wise self-consistency learning with an inconsistency image generator, arXiv:2012.09311 (checked via search). PW-MAD pixel-wise supervision with uniform maps (memory). Majumdar et al., partial tampering of faces, CVPRW 2019 (seen in search results).

ideas.title: Counterfactual-pair erasure: remove only what label-preserving interventions move, then a linear head
ideas.mechanism: Collect pairs of the same image before and after an intervention that cannot change the label and that already exists on disk: SMDD renders and their shrunk copies (A47 data), FFHQ photos native and E7, later photo versus reconstruction if the ruling allows. Fit a closed-form linear eraser on the final features so that processed versus unprocessed is linearly unpredictable, keep it as a fixed layer of the single network, and train a linear head on the erased features. Before any training, measure the cosine between the history direction and the morph-versus-genuine direction: if they are collinear the problem is intrinsic to the backbone.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Strong sense, for a linear head: after erasure no linear read-out, whatever labels or loss it was trained with, can use the erased intervention on the fitting distribution, so a confounded training set cannot bring the cue back. Because the eraser is fitted on same-image pairs and never on class labels, it cannot delete the morph label unless the two directions coincide, which is measured. Neutralised: resampling history at the fitted doses; JPEG, decoding steps and renderer only if pairs exist. Not neutralised: any non-linear use (so the final head must stay linear and the eraser must be refitted after any backbone update), interventions without pairs, and out-of-distribution pools unless tested. History erasure needs no ruling; renderer erasure requires the ruling that a one-photo reconstruction is a processed genuine image, and must not be done if it is ruled manipulated.
ideas.covers: All three families for genuine-side history (the E7 collapse on diffusion cells is the target). Renderer fingerprint for GAN and diffusion only under the reconstruction ruling. Does not create any morph signal.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Features of a few thousand pairs from /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a47/data47/i3 and the A46 FFHQ pools, plus AR1, about 20 GPU-minutes; the eraser is a covariance computation. Stress tests: (i) train the A47 morph-free task (render versus shrunk copy, which reached 0.00 to 1.17 % EER on MorDIFF and DiM without seeing a morph) on erased features: it must be at chance on held-out pairs and must no longer pass MorDIFF; (ii) train a head on native genuine versus morphs and test under E7. Evaluate invariance on the 204 FRLL photos by 7 existing variants, which are test persons and never used for fitting.
ideas.falsifier: Absolute cosine between whitened history and morph directions above 0.5; or after erasure the genuine score still shifts by more than 0.2 pooled SD under resmatch on FRLL (AUC native versus E7 outside 0.44 to 0.56); or morph-versus-genuine AUC on AR1 falls by more than 0.03; or the erased morph-free head still gets below 30 % EER on MorDIFF.
ideas.compute: About 20 GPU-minutes of feature extraction, then CPU minutes.
ideas.main_risk: Three projection attempts by the Codex loop on 10 Nov failed their joint criterion (projection N, geometry-overlap weighting, a 9-direction geometry nullspace: twin AUC and camera AUC traded off), and per-image token normalisation left processing decodable. Those removed directions estimated from class-linked contrasts; this removes only same-image intervention directions and claims no gain in twin AUC, but the prior odds are low and transfer of the eraser from SMDD and FFHQ to studio photos is unproven.
ideas.closest_prior_work: LEACE, arXiv:2306.03819 (checked via search). INLP (memory). Codex renderer-direction projection, geometry nullspace and Astra E2 (record, read this session). A49 consistency loss, failed (record).

ideas.title: Common-sign direction across pipelines, with a certificate when none exists
ideas.mechanism: Call each tool or generator crossed with each source set an environment. In each, compute within-set feature differences (morph minus its matched genuine image) on frozen features. Solve a small convex programme for the unit direction that maximises the smallest standardised within-set margin over environments. If the optimum is at or below zero there is no linear evidence shared by all environments, and that is a certificate, not a failed training run; leave-one-environment-out gives the honest transfer number.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: A feature whose within-set effect is zero or reversed in at least one environment cannot raise the objective, so generator-specific traces are excluded by the objective itself; the Codex heads showed exactly such reversals (trained on StyleGAN3 reconstructions as negatives, AUC 0.26 to 0.32 on DiffAE, while same-person negatives transferred weakly positive, 0.57 to 0.67, on 8 to 15 diagnostic pairs). Benchmark-construction cues are constant within sets and never enter. Not neutralised: a cue present with the same sign in every environment (one clean environment is required), and small-sample noise. Under the ruling that reconstructions are processed genuine the contrasts are reconstruction versus morph; if they are ruled manipulated the question becomes camera versus render and the environments must be rebuilt with history-matched camera photos.
ideas.covers: Landmark, GAN and diffusion together; it answers whether any family-independent single-image morph evidence exists in a given backbone. It cannot cover a family with no matched sets on disk (MIPGAN until AG1).
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: Existing sets only: AR1 (2 tools by 2 sources), GAN32 and trainplus blocks, DiffAE expanded123, H4b (338 MIPGAN-style morphs versus host renders). CLIP ViT-L/14 and DINOv3 features, about 15 GPU-minutes, then CPU. Stress test: plant a grey corner square on the morphs of all environments but one; the max-min direction must give it zero weight while a pooled cross-entropy head uses it.
ideas.falsifier: Max-min standardised margin at or below 0.2 (worst-environment AUC about 0.56) with bootstrap upper bound below 0.35 (AUC about 0.60): no universal linear evidence in that backbone, so drop cross-family claims and write the limit. A leave-one-family-out AUC below 0.60 on the held-out family says the same.
ideas.compute: About 15 GPU-minutes plus CPU minutes.
ideas.main_risk: With 64 to 102 blocks per generator the estimate is noisy, and the likely outcome is the negative certificate, which serves the measured-limit paper but not a method claim.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Invariant Risk Minimization, arXiv:1907.02893 (checked via search). Risk extrapolation, arXiv:2003.00688 (memory). Group DRO (memory). Codex multigenerator DRO, 10 heads (record).

ideas.title: Spatially centred log band-energy stream: invariance to global filtering by algebra
ideas.mechanism: Replace the frequency stream's absolute band energies by local log band energies with the spatial mean of each band subtracted, and read only bands below a fixed cut-off set by the smallest native face size in scope. A global blur or resampling kernel multiplies each band by one number everywhere, which becomes a constant in the log and is removed exactly by the centring; bands above the cut-off are never read by any input. What remains is the spatial pattern of relative texture energy, which a blend changes locally (aligned edges keep contrast, unaligned texture loses about 3 dB) and a global filter does not.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Strong sense, by architecture: the stream's features are unchanged by any global linear shift-invariant filtering that is non-zero below the cut-off, and by anything at all above it, for every input and regardless of training data. That covers the shrink-and-enlarge history up to the cut-off dose. Not neutralised: JPEG (block-wise, not a global filter), renderer fingerprints, noise-floor effects, and any cue in the spatial branch if one is kept beside it. It removes the absolute sharpness level, which the record identified as the old stream's shortcut. Needs confirmation that a fixed analysis filter bank inside the network is not counted as new blur code; no other ruling.
ideas.covers: Landmark morphs (best for splice-type families with an unblended reference region; weaker for full-frame blends). Not GAN or diffusion morphs.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: CPU only, about 1 hour: fixed band energies (8 bands, 32 by 32 windows) on AR1 rungs and on the 204 FRLL photos by 7 existing variants; logistic head with matched-set training. Read R2 versus R4 AUC on FRLL persons and the score shift under blur1, resample50 and both resmatch variants (expected about 0 by construction; jpeg50 is expected to move). Stress test: train a head on native genuine versus shrunk copies with these features; it must stay at chance.
ideas.falsifier: R2 versus R4 AUC below 0.70 on FRLL persons, or a shift above 0.2 pooled SD under resmatch_mordiff, or the confounded head above 0.60.
ideas.compute: CPU, about 1 hour including coding.
ideas.main_risk: Hand-made spectral features are weak next to CLIP features, and a single-stream detector built on them will not be state of the art; its use is as a provably invariant auxiliary stream or as the MADMamba side arm. The narrow-band approximation and aliasing leave a residual that has to be measured.
ideas.closest_prior_work: MADMamba frequency stream findings E07, A18, A19, A22 (record). FD-MAD and SRL-MAD region-wise spectral residuals, arXiv:2601.20656 and arXiv:2603.15050 (as listed in the record, not re-opened). PRNU variance analysis for morph detection, Debiasi et al., BTAS 2018 (checked via search). Local phase quantisation as a blur-insensitive descriptor and log-spectrum processing (memory).

objections_to_current_plan: Twins give only the weak guarantee. Matching removes the incentive to use a cue but nothing makes the score invariant at test. Training is on lossless PNG twins with one history (no new resize or compression code is allowed), while benchmark cells differ in history by class, so the E7 response of a twin-trained head is unconstrained. Frozen CLIP tokens carry the history (Astra E2: resmatch decodable at AUC 1.0), and the existing CLIP ViT-L/14 probe trained on morph versus reconstruction already leaked on its reconstruction control (0.597, upper bound above 0.60). The plan has no mechanism for this, only a guard (G2).

The landmark R2 rung is degenerate. AR1's own pre-registration records that OpenCV on one photo is bit-identical to the photo and FaceMorpher differs by at most 1 grey level in about 14 % of pixels. So the main verdict R2 versus R4 equals photo versus morph, the condition 'R0 to R2 share at most 0.2' passes trivially, and a detector that keys on any warp-and-average smoothing is labelled 'reads morphing'.

The twin contrast R3 versus R4 is confounded with warp size. The Codex loop found that rendering geometry alone predicted the class at AUC 0.81 pooled and 0.92 on FERET, and its three post hoc fixes failed. The plan answers with post hoc bins (G1); a design that crosses or matches geometry is available and costs CPU minutes.

Image-level cross-entropy on pooled families is exposed to imbalance between matched sets: same-person morphs exist only for multi-session sources, graded sets add positives for 300 hosts, and generator panels are 64 to 102 blocks against 536 landmark hosts. Any family or source cue then predicts the label. Use a within-set likelihood or exact balancing.

Novelty of twin training is overstated. MorDeephy (arXiv:2208.03110, checked this session) trained a single-image detector with about 500k same-person selfmorphs labelled bona fide, explicitly to reduce reliance on blending artefacts; MorphGuard (arXiv:2505.10497, checked) reuses it. 03_LITERATURE lists MorDeephy as 'method not re-read' and rates M1 novelty medium-high. The paper cannot present twin negatives as new for landmark morphs; its labelling is also the opposite of the author's ruling that same-person morphs are morphs.

Under the author's ruling the main label (two captures blended) and the side label (two identities) are different causal variables. One image-level head trained on R2 versus R4 will learn the easier one, noise and texture averaging, which is close to what blur and resampling do to a genuine photo. The verdict rules reward that. A non-trivial one-photo rung and the score shifts under the existing FRLL variants (jpeg50, resample50, blur1, resmatch) belong in the pass criteria.

For GAN morphs the plan's main contrast (reconstruction versus morph) will be met by latent averageness, which alone separates H3 at AUC 1.000 and is read by a linear probe at 0.91, while the cue matrix lists averageness as a cue (row 18). The plan must state whether averageness is the legitimate signal (for a latent average it is the only causal trace) or a shortcut; without that the GAN verdict cannot be interpreted. The open ruling on reconstructions has the same effect.

Gate G-c is biased towards 'not readable'. gate_c.py groups folds by host only, but the partner photo of a test morph is the second photo of a person whose twin sits in a training fold with label 0. With 1,024 features and about 850 training images the probe can fit photo-specific directions and push the test morph towards 'twin'. Folds must hold out both persons of every morph.

No experiment in the plan plants a confound on purpose. Guards G1 to G4 look for named cues after the fact. A flip test (train with a planted cue, test with it reversed) costs minutes and is the only direct evidence that a training design ignores cues it was not told about.
invariance.first_experiment_tonight: Two steps on existing assets, about 3 hours in total. Step 0 (zero GPU, 45 minutes): (a) identity-dose audit: per release and per benchmark family, Spearman between morph score (A12REL scores_eval.npz) and contributor distance from FRLL embeddings, with the face-recognition oracle as power check; decision: slope of 0.2 or more with lower bound above 0 on landmark families and about 0 on diffusion and GAN means the 'landmark yes, generators no' paper is already measured; flat everywhere with oracle power means even the E7-robust CLIP rows do not read identity. (b) geometry-only classifier R3 versus R4 from the AR1 landmark files; above 0.65 means the present twin contrast is confounded. Step 1 (DGX, about 2 hours): build R2w (and R2g) for the 536 + 102 AR1 hosts with the unchanged OpenCV and FaceMorpher tools; extract frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 and DINOv3 ViT-L/16 features for all AR1 rungs and for the 204 FRLL photos by 7 existing variants; train linear heads with cross-entropy and with the matched-set likelihood, folds holding out both persons, with the planted grey-corner confound at 9 to 1. Read four numbers on FRLL persons: R2w versus R4 AUC (go at 0.80 or more), R3 versus R4 AUC on the left-out tool (signal if lower bound above 0.55), flip gap (cross-entropy expected above 0.2, matched-set must be at most 0.03), and genuine-score shift under resmatch_mordiff (pass at most 0.2 pooled SD; otherwise run the erasure idea next).
invariance.detectability_analysis: Landmark (pixel blend after warp): three causal traces. (a) Two captures averaged: independent sensor noise and fine texture lose about 3 dB inside the blended area at every frequency while landmark-aligned edges keep their contrast; this separates a one-photo image from any morph, including a same-person morph, and a global blur imitates only its absolute level, not the pattern. (b) Second identity: person-specific detail (brows, iris, nostrils, lip line, moles, skin tone) appears doubled at half contrast; this separates same-person from two-person morphs, grows with contributor distance and vanishes for look-alikes. (c) Warp size: larger for two people, but also for pose differences, so it is fragile. Not detectable: (a) once the image is low-passed below the texture band (E7 at about 3 times), and any within-image contrast when the whole frame is blended. GAN latent average: one coherent face, no local double structure. The only causal trace is position in latent space, closer to the mean by sqrt((1+c)/2). With the latent it separates H3 at 1.000, a linear probe reads 0.91, and single-person renders matched in spread are indistinguishable (0.42 to 0.52), because such a render is itself an averaged identity. So detectable means averageness at population level; identity mixing as such, look-alike pairs, and transfer of the averageness direction between generators are not shown. Diffusion (semantic code interpolation plus noise-map interpolation): no pixel blend; traces are averageness of the code, interpolated stochastic detail and decoder schedule. Inside one generator, morph versus reconstruction is linearly readable from frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 (0.993 cross-fitted on FRLL persons, 0.81 to 0.95 on DiM families, E7 control 0.48), same-person versus two-person only 0.65 to 0.86 on small panels, and nothing transfers across generators so far. If the author rules that a reconstruction is manipulated, GAN and diffusion detection becomes render detection and the only shortcut left is the history of the genuine photos.
invariance.sota_definition: Shortcut-free, relative to a listed cue set, means three measured properties. Design: in the training data each listed cue is independent of the supervised target within its matched set or image (randomised, crossed or constant by construction), checked by a cue-only classifier at AUC 0.45 to 0.55. Score: for every label-preserving intervention available on disk (E7 at each dose, jpeg50, resample50, blur1, chip, one-photo warp, decoding steps) the genuine-image score moves by at most 0.2 pooled SD (AUC between intervened and original within 0.44 to 0.56), on FRLL and on one pool that is not FRLL. Flip: trained on a deliberately confounded set, the flip gap is at most 0.03. State of the art means one network, five seeds, mean with interval, ranked by the worst case over native and E7 genuine photos, never by native numbers: on corrected MAD22 and the FRLL cells no worse than the released MADation ViT-L/14 under the same worst case (reference under E7: 1.0 / 1.0 / 14.7 / 4.4 % EER on the FRLL landmark families, 9.8 % on Greedy-DiM), and on the ladder's main contrast (processed one-photo image versus two-person morph) AUC of 0.90 or more on a held-out tool with FRLL persons, with the genuine rejection rate at 10 % missed attacks printed.

Spread-matched single-person renders (X4 type) as the GAN genuine class or as a pass criterion: they are averaged-identity images by construction.
'R0 to R2 share at most 0.2' as a pass condition for landmark tools until a non-degenerate one-photo rung exists.

LoRA runs and five-seed matrices before the linear-head tests of tonight pass; those tests take minutes and decide what is worth five seeds.

The claim 'first twin-trained S-MAD detector' (MorDeephy, 2022).

ideas.title: Pixel-free training: the attack class is made by embedding arithmetic (virtual morphs), and the same fit gives the identity ceiling
ideas.mechanism: Use a frozen face-recognition (FR) network at its 112-pixel input and keep only the unit-length embedding. Build the classes without any morph image: a virtual morph is the normalised sum of the embeddings of two photos of different persons, a virtual twin is the normalised sum of two photos of one person, genuine is a single embedding. Fit a small head on millions of such triples from FRGC, colorFERET and CASIA persons, then score real images. In this space the only first-order difference is that a morph's component along the population mean grows by kappa = sqrt(2/(1+c)), c being the cosine of the two sources (1.39 for a random pair, 1.27 at the AR1 median c = 0.23, 1.15 at c = 0.5, 1.03 for a twin), so the best possible AUC is Phi((kappa_morph - kappa_negative) x Lambda / sqrt 2), Lambda = Mahalanobis length of the population mean. The in-domain virtual AUC per similarity bin is the measured ceiling for any identity-only reader.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: The attack class has no pixels during training, so no tool, generator, file or history property can correlate with the label. At test time everything passes through a 112-pixel identity crop. The record's only FR-space probe had controls at 0.506 (native vs E7 photos) and 0.493 (reconstruction vs aligner copy), where a CLIP probe read 0.597 (A46 d2). The failure mode is visible, not hidden: if real morph embeddings do not lie near the normalised sum of their sources, the head does not fire.
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes if fidelity holds (to be measured tonight; an older in-house number implies about 0.74). Diffusion (DiffAE, MorDIFF, DiM): yes in principle; the existing probe reads 0.59 to 0.68. GAN: only potent morphs, nothing for re-normalised or length-restored codes. Everywhere the ceiling is about 0.65 to 0.80 AUC at benchmark-like pair similarity (Lambda 2 to 4), so this is the identity component and a bound, not a high-accuracy detector on its own.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: GEO-0, CPU only, about 30 minutes, every embedding already exists (glintr100). Files: /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/fr_emb_built.npz (built R3, R4, NC, 534/532/534 per tool, plus FRLL 102 each), /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/pool_src_emb.npz and frll_src_emb.npz (source photos H, S, R), experiments/AR1/pool.csv (pairs), /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a46/feat/a46_feat.npz (5,146 embeddings: FRLL gallery 'raw', a43_B, a43_D, rec, published MorDIFF and three DiM families, native and E7 controls). Steps: (1) fidelity F = cos(embedding of the built image, normalised sum of its two source embeddings), separately for R3 and R4 and for a43_B and the published diffusion morphs; (2) mean-direction projection of R4 and R3 relative to the host photo against the predictions 1.27 and 1.03; (3) head fitted on virtual morphs and twins of FRGC and colorFERET source embeddings only (5 folds by person), applied unchanged to AR1 R4 vs R3 and R4 vs host photo, a43_B vs a43_D, published families vs rec, with controls native vs E7 and rec vs a256; (4) Lambda and the ceiling per cosine bin. Go: at least 0.65 with lower bound above 0.60 on both AR1 (R4 vs R3) and a43_B vs a43_D, controls inside 0.45 to 0.55.
ideas.falsifier: Virtual-trained head at or below 0.55 (upper bound below 0.60) on both AR1 R4 vs R3 and a43_B vs a43_D while its in-domain virtual AUC is at least 0.70: real morphs do not follow the midpoint law in FR space, drop the idea and keep only the ceiling. Any control outside 0.45 to 0.55: the by-construction claim is false.
ideas.compute: Tonight: CPU, about 30 minutes. Full version: glintr100 on about 50,000 CASIA crops and 8,000 FRGC and colorFERET frames, under 1 GPU-hour; heads in minutes; five seeds are trivial.
ideas.main_risk: Low ceiling. Fidelity may erase or flip the sign: at F = 0.74 the mean-direction gain 1.27 becomes 0.94. A 536-person pool is too small to estimate a 512-dimensional mean and covariance (CASIA is needed for a stable Lambda). The head may learn a dataset centre instead of a midpoint (check by leaving one photo source out). The FR network may have seen CASIA persons in its own training (not verified).
ideas.closest_prior_work: Record, checked this session: A46 d2 glint probe, 0.682 [0.612, 0.752] on held-out DiffAE morphs vs reconstructions with fold models trained on 53 to 85 images, 0.59 to 0.65 on published families (smadcvpr/results/A46/a46_d2.md). ideas/IDEAS_v1.md M2 and E3 (read after I formed this list): a morph-free between-person read-out and a ceiling curve; the difference here is training the detector itself on virtual morphs and virtual twins, the unit-sphere formula, and the fidelity check. Kessler, Raja, Tapia, Busch, arXiv 2305.18216 (checked, abstract page): FR embeddings as detection features, trained on real morph images. Colbois, Otroshi Shahreza, Marcel, arXiv 2402.00695 (checked, abstract page): the optimal morph embedding is the average of the source embeddings, used to generate attacks. Otroshi Shahreza et al., IEEE TIFS 2025 and Kelly et al., arXiv 2111.15416 (search results only). Manifold mixup (memory). Two searches found no detector trained on embedding-space morphs; that is not proof of absence.

ideas.title: Shrink-law audit on the published benchmark morphs, from scores that already exist
ideas.mechanism: Inside one benchmark family all morphs share tool, format, size and history, so a detector that reads those gives every morph the same expected score. An identity reader must score a morph higher when its two contributors are less alike, because the identity loss is L = 2a(1-a)(1 - cos(A, B)). For every released detector and family, compute the rank correlation between the morph score and 1 - cos(A, B), with the pair taken from the file name and the cosine from glintr100 embeddings of the 204 FRLL photos. The same number is then demanded of our own detector. This is an identity test on the benchmark cells themselves, with thousands of morphs and no new image.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: The comparison is morph against morph inside one construction. Genuine photos and their history are not involved, so no genuine-side cue can create a slope. The only alternative explanation is a pair-dependent tool effect (ghosting grows with dissimilarity in landmark tools); that is a morph trace, not a benchmark cue, and it is separated by reading the generator families, where there is no ghosting.
ideas.covers: Audit of released detectors in all three families (FRLL-Morphs five families of about 1,200 morphs, MAD22 five families, MorDIFF 1,000, six DiM families of 500), and a required check for our own detector in all three.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: CPU, under one hour. Scores: smadcvpr_runs/A12_scored/A12REL/<release>/scores_eval.npz (MADation ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14, SelfMAD in our pipeline), experiments/A32-RSX_resolution-shortcut/raw/selfmad_own_eval.npz, and the A12BR recipe rows. Embeddings: group 'raw' in /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a46/feat/a46_feat.npz. Statistic: Spearman per family with the two-way person bootstrap of a41_read.py, computed inside neutral-neutral and smiling-smiling pairs because expression is unbalanced in 11 of 17 cells (C1). Power check: the same correlation for the reference-based oracle score and for the virtual-trained head of idea 1. Corrected MAD22 scores do not exist yet (job 6299123 pending), so MAD22 uses the old subset and is labelled so.
ideas.falsifier: For a detector's identity reading: correlation upper bound at or below +0.10 in every generator family means no identity reading there. For the tool itself: if the reference-based oracle's own correlation is below 0.3 in a family, the similarity range there is too narrow and the audit is void for that family.
ideas.compute: CPU minutes. No GPU.
ideas.main_risk: Benchmark pairs were chosen to look alike, so the similarity range may be narrow. File names may not expose the pair in every family (not verified for FRLL-Morphs, MorDIFF and DiM). In landmark families a positive slope can come from ghost size, which is morph evidence but not identity evidence. MAD22 on the old subset only.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Plan items AR7 and M3(ii) and IDEAS_v1 E5 (a response surface on our own AR1 builds); this uses the published morphs and existing scores. Record, checked: A39 R1 (PROTOCOL.md l.12240 to 12306) reports within-class correlations of recipe networks' scores with code distance from the average face of +0.04 to +0.24 on the StyleGAN3 set, the opposite sign to an identity reader (descriptive, no verdict). Kessler et al., arXiv 2305.18216 (checked, abstract page): similar pairs make stronger attacks. I found no published within-class identity audit of detectors (not an exhaustive search).

ideas.title: Distil the reference-based oracle: one scalar identity-displacement target in place of two recovered identities
ideas.mechanism: The record has an oracle that separates morphs from one-person images almost perfectly when it may see the source photos (0.998 in AR1 gate G-b, 1.000 in AD1 and A46 d2) and that is blind to history (0.501 native vs E7). Train an image-only student to regress that oracle's value for each training image: d = 1 - cos(FR(image), FR(a host photo not used in the build)), or the theoretical L where sources are known. The teacher sees references, the student never does. Direction recovery is impossible, magnitude is the only identifiable part, so this replaces the two-identity head. The target is 0 for R0, R1, R2, about 0.07 for same-person morphs at the AR1 medians, about 0.38 for two-person morphs, and graded with the mixing fraction.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: The target varies inside each pipeline (with pair similarity and mixing fraction), so 'the tool was used' explains only a step. The number that counts is the partial correlation inside R4 at mixing 0.5 on a held-out tool, where history is constant. The teacher's own controls show it carries no history.
ideas.covers: Landmark: plausible, because superposition strength grows with the same quantity. Diffusion and GAN: only up to the typicality ceiling, expected weak. It labels non-potent generator 'morphs' as near genuine, which is the correct label.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: On AR1 as built today: frozen features (CLIP ViT-L/14, DINOv3-L, glintr100 maps) of R2, R3, R4, NC for 536 hosts and two tools, plus the graded FaceMorpher set (300 hosts, six mixing levels). Teacher values from /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/fr_emb_built.npz and pool_src_emb.npz. Ridge and two-layer heads, 5 folds by person, train on one tool and test on the other. Read: R2 vs R4 AUC beside a binary head on the same folds; Spearman between prediction and teacher value inside R4 at mixing 0.5; R0 vs R1 on FRLL native and E7 frames.
ideas.falsifier: Held-out-tool correlation inside R4 with lower bound at or below 0.10, or R2 vs R4 AUC more than 0.03 below the binary head, or R0 vs R1 above 0.60.
ideas.compute: Feature cache under 1 GPU-hour (shared with other tests), heads in minutes; a LoRA confirmation is about 1 hour per seed.
ideas.main_risk: AR1 pairs are look-alikes (median cosine 0.23), so the target range inside R4 is narrow; a random-pair arm is needed (CPU build). The student may read ghost size, which correlates with the target. Under the ruling R3 is an attack, while this target puts it near genuine, so it should be an auxiliary output or the side-study score, not the main label.
ideas.closest_prior_work: IDEAS_v1 M5 (shrink-factor regression from source cosines; read after I formed mine). Differences: the target is the measured oracle value of the actual image, which accounts for imperfect rendering and for potency, and the framing as learning with privileged references. In-house negatives for direction recovery, checked this session: the two-identity demorph head S8 (divergence-only EER 0.63 to 0.74 on FRLL, mambamorph-code/EXPERIMENTS.md l.479 to 497) and the reference-free demorpher (0.00 to 0.27% strict recovery against 97 to 99% for the oracle, /home/narolski/demorpher/results/headline.md). Learning using privileged information and generalised distillation (memory). DiffusionFake, OrthoMAD, IDistill (as marked in 03_LITERATURE_AND_METHODS.md, not reopened).

ideas.title: Identity coherence in a face-recognition trunk: two photos of one person add up, two persons cancel
ideas.mechanism: An FR network responds to features that persist across photos of one person. In a blend of two photos of one person those features coincide; in a blend of two persons they do not. If the network were linear in the blend, the unnormalised response would have relative length sqrt((1+cos)/2): 0.97 for the AR1 twins (cosine 0.87) and 0.79 for the AR1 morphs (cosine 0.23), a 19% gap, and the part of the embedding outside the span of the two sources (the span deficit, 1 - F squared) would be larger for morphs. Measure both with no training, then read the trunk's feature maps with a small head trained on the genuine constructions against R4 and R3.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: The trunk sees a 112-pixel crop, below the bands where the benchmark history lives (controls 0.506 and 0.493 in A46 d2). The raw amplitude is NOT safe: feature norm is a quality proxy by design, so it is used only as a mechanism test between twins and morphs of one pipeline, never as a stand-alone score. The trained head must pass R0 vs R1 and R0 vs R2 silence.
ideas.covers: Landmark: yes (pixel superposition). DiffAE-type diffusion: weak, one coherent render. GAN: no.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: No training, about 20 GPU-minutes: unnormalised glintr100 output (and the AdaFace IR-101 under /home/narolski/demorpher/weights) on /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/img/frgcferet/{opencv,facemorpher}/{R3,R4,NC} and the source frames. Read: AUC of the norm for R3 vs R4 and source vs R4; span deficit for R3 and R4; the same on A43 C20 vs B20 and on the GAN32 roles SA/SB vs P0/P1; silence on FRLL native vs E7 frames. Then heads on layer-3 and layer-4 maps, leaving one tool out.
ideas.falsifier: Norm AUC for R3 vs R4 below 0.60 on both tools and no difference in span deficit (interval includes 0): there is no coherence effect and the trunk adds only band-limiting. For the head: R2 vs R4 on the held-out tool below 0.70, or R0 vs R1 above 0.60.
ideas.compute: Minutes to 1 GPU-hour for the probes and heads; a LoRA fit about 1 hour.
ideas.main_risk: Network nonlinearity may hide the effect. At 112 pixels fine superposition is gone. The norm reacts to blur and compression, so a head can relearn quality. Licences of the FR weights.
ideas.closest_prior_work: IDEAS_v1 M4 proposes the 112-pixel FR backbone for its blindness (read after I formed mine); added here are the coherence prediction with numbers, the span deficit, and the ban on the raw norm. Fu and Damer, arXiv 2208.05864 (checked, abstract page): MagFace and quality scores as unsupervised detection, over 70% accuracy; the abstract states no matched one-person control. AdaFace, arXiv 2204.00964 (search result only): feature norm tracks image quality. Kessler et al., arXiv 2305.18216 (checked, abstract page). Scherhag et al., arXiv 2001.01202 (search result only): FR features for differential detection.

ideas.title: Is the morph a mosaic? A reference-based oracle that decides whether any part-wise identity method can work
ideas.mechanism: For a uniform blend, the expected identity agreement between two face regions equals the genuine level to first order: for regions r and s it is (g + i)/sqrt((1+c_r)(1+c_s)), with g the genuine and i the impostor part agreement, which is g for unrelated pairs. Part-wise agreement therefore has no first-order signal. It drops (by at most 50%) only if regions lean to different contributors, which splice morphs do by construction and generator morphs might do if facial attributes snap to one parent. Measure the leaning with the sources in hand: per-region FR embeddings (all but one region blanked with the approved constant colour) of the morph and of both contributors, dominance d_r = cos(M_r, A_r) - cos(M_r, B_r), and the between-region variance of d_r relative to twins and to the negative-control twin. Build a reference-free score only where the oracle shows a mosaic.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Agreement between regions of one image is a comparison inside the image; filtering, compression and resampling act on all regions alike. The oracle step uses no detector.
ideas.covers: Splice-type landmark morphs (AMSL-like): expected yes. Full-face landmark, GAN, diffusion: expected no; this test turns that expectation into a measured limit per family.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: About 15 GPU-minutes of FR forward passes: six regions (each eye, nose, mouth, inner face, outer face) for A43 B20 (200) and C20 (102) with FRLL sources, h3_sg3 morphs (423) with their CASIA source crops, FRLL-Morphs AMSL with FRLL sources, and AR1 R4, R3, NC (OpenCV). Masks from existing landmarks (.tem files or prep_eval.kps).
ideas.falsifier: Variance ratio morph over twin below 1.2 with upper bound below 1.5: part-wise methods are closed for that family, including the plan's part-wise item. Go only at 1.5 or more.
ideas.compute: Minutes.
ideas.main_risk: Embeddings of heavily blanked faces are noisy, so the oracle may lack power: first check that region embeddings verify their own source (part genuine cosine at least 0.2). Even a full mosaic gives a modest ceiling, roughly 0.65 to 0.75.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Identity consistency transformer for face swaps (Dong et al., CVPR 2022, memory) uses inner against outer identity. Plan item M7 in 03_LITERATURE_AND_METHODS.md. The D-MAD log D42 lists inner/outer completion as pre-empted (record, checked). Ferrara, Franco, Maltoni, BIOSIG 2019 (search result only) separate shape and texture when building morphs. I have not seen the zero-first-order argument or an oracle-first test.

ideas.title: Twins made inside the network: average the token sequences of two persons against two photos of one person
ideas.mechanism: Positions in an aligned crop correspond across faces, so two images can be blended inside a vision transformer by averaging their token sequences at a chosen layer and running the remaining layers. Attack class: mixed tokens of two persons. Genuine class: mixed tokens of two photos of one person, and unmixed images. No tool, no generator, no file; unlimited pairs from FRGC, colorFERET and CASIA with every person under both labels. The mixing layer is chosen by measurement: the layer at which a real morph's tokens are best explained by the average of its sources' tokens. At the last layer this reduces to idea 1; at the first layer it is an unwarped pixel blend.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Both classes come from the same in-network operation on the same photo pools, so the only class difference is whether the two inputs are one person. Every real tool and generator is then a held-out test, which answers the objection that training data and audit rungs share build scripts.
ideas.covers: Landmark: plausible at early and middle layers. Diffusion and GAN: only typicality at late layers; a coherent render does not look like a token average, so no gain beyond idea 1 is expected.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: About 2 GPU-hours on the DGX: frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 (cached) and, if it loads, the AdaFace ViT under /home/narolski/demorpher/weights; mixing at layer 0, one third, two thirds and last; 20,000 mixed pairs from the AR1 candidate frames (6,921 frames; training persons outside the 536 hosts); linear head on the pooled output; test on real AR1 R4 vs R3 and R4 vs R2 for both tools and on A43 B20 vs C20 and D20. The layer is fixed by token-level fit on 100 AR1 morphs before any head is scored.
ideas.falsifier: Best layer below 0.60 on real R4 vs R3 for both tools while the in-distribution AUC is at least 0.90: in-network mixtures do not resemble real morphs; drop.
ideas.compute: About 2 GPU-hours for heads; LoRA about 1 hour per seed.
ideas.main_risk: Unwarped mixing produces geometric ghosting that real morphs remove, so the head may learn ghost size (the pose-gap guard applies). Late-layer mixtures are off the image manifold. It needs the author's word on whether in-network mixing counts as a new morphing path.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Manifold mixup (memory). Self-blended images and SelfMAD (as marked in 03_LITERATURE_AND_METHODS.md) blend one image with itself in pixel space and call it an attack; here one-person mixtures are genuine, two-person mixtures are attacks, and nothing is rendered. Pimenta et al., arXiv 2309.00549 (as cited in IDEAS_v1, not opened by me) label tool-made same-person morphs genuine.

ideas.title: Potency-conditioned evaluation and the potency against detectability frontier
ideas.mechanism: A morph is an attack only if it matches both contributors. In the record this share ranges from 99% (our DiffAE and AR1 landmark builds) through 66% (Poisson set H1) and 48% (StyleGAN3 set H3) to about 1% (IP-Adapter midpoint set H2). Report every ladder cell on the potent subset (both contributors verified at a false match rate of 1 in 1,000 with photos not used in the build), list non-potent 'morphs' separately, and plot per family the attack strength and the identity ceiling against contributor similarity. The plot shows where benchmark pairs sit: random pairs are visible to an identity reader but weak against strict thresholds, look-alike pairs are strong and nearly invisible to identity.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: It removes a hidden construction variable: a detector is neither credited nor blamed for images that are not attacks, and 'GAN morph detection' on non-potent sets is shown to be generator detection by definition.
ideas.covers: Evaluation for all families; most consequential for GAN cells.
ideas.cheapest_decisive_test: CPU, under one hour: the potency columns cos_/mcos_{glint,w600k}_{a,b} already sit in the manifests of h1_poisson, h2_embmid, h3_sg3, h4_mipgan1, arc2face and a43; for published DiM and MorDIFF morphs compute them from a46_feat.npz (published morph embeddings and the FRLL gallery, fresh photo = the other expression); re-read the AD1 and AG5 score files on the potent subset; ceiling from idea 1.
ideas.falsifier: If every verdict and every AUC changes by less than 0.02 between all morphs and potent morphs in all families, potency conditioning is not needed (A41 found this for the StyleGAN3 set) and only the frontier plot is kept.
ideas.compute: CPU minutes.
ideas.main_risk: FRLL has two frontal photos per person, so the fresh photo differs in expression. Thresholds depend on the FR model. Embeddings of the published FRLL-Morphs and MAD22 morphs need a 10-minute extraction.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Mated morph presentation match rate (Scherhag et al., 2017, memory) and Morphing Attack Potential (Ferrara, Franco, Maltoni, Busch, 2022, memory) measure attack strength in vulnerability studies. Conditioning detector evaluation on it and placing it beside a detectability ceiling I have not seen. Kessler et al., arXiv 2305.18216 (checked, abstract page): pre-selected similar pairs make stronger attacks.

objections_to_current_plan: The two-identity recovery head (T5) is predicted to fail and has already failed twice in the author's own record: the two-identity demorph head S8 (divergence-only EER 0.63 to 0.74 on FRLL) and the reference-free demorpher (0.00 to 0.27% strict recovery against 97 to 99% for the oracle). Given the morph embedding, the difference between the contributors is uniformly distributed around it, so no head can beat the morph's own embedding at finding them. It should be dropped outright, not merely placed in the cut order.

The plan has no image-only ceiling. Gate G-b uses the source photos, so it shows that the morphs are potent, not that a single image carries a readable signal. Without a ceiling, a null on generator cells cannot be told apart from a weak detector, and gate G-c (probe readability) was not run in AD1 or AG5.

The verdict bar 'reads morphing: AUC at least 0.75 on R2 vs R4' is probably above the identity ceiling for generator cells at benchmark pair similarity (my estimate 0.65 to 0.78 for the AR1 median pair, 0.59 to 0.67 for strong look-alikes). On those cells the rule is either unreachable or, if reached, a warning sign that something other than identity is being read (smoother interpolated output, expression mixing, pose gap).

The stated reason for choosing CLIP ViT-L/14 as the base (the release does not move under E7 on Greedy-DiM) is weakened by today's AD1 re-read: on MorDIFF the same release has an R0 to R2 share of 1.24 [0.94, 1.73], R2 vs R4 at 0.486, and at its benchmark threshold flags 51% of history-matched photos and 82% of one-photo reconstructions. The only read-out in the record with clean history controls and a non-zero signal is the FR-embedding probe of A46 d2 (0.68, controls 0.506 and 0.493), and it was fitted on 53 to 85 images per fold. An FR-space arm is missing from T4.

The 'typicality' item T3 pools three different things: FR feature norm (a quality measure by design, so a history cue), the CLIP typicality direction (averageness of the whole image; truncated renders are separable by simple image properties at 0.96, A37) and the direction of the identity embedding. Only the last is identity. On the unit sphere the 'thin shell' argument does not apply, so FR-space ceilings are far lower than a shell calculation with 30 identity dimensions suggests.

Twins and morphs in AR1 differ in source cosine (0.87 against 0.23) and in everything that travels with it (ghost size, pose and shape gap). R3 vs R4 therefore cannot separate identity from ghost magnitude. A within-R4 dose in contributor similarity and a random-pair arm are needed; AR7 does part of this and is on the cut list.

Potency is not conditioned. Verdicts on sets where half or more of the 'morphs' do not carry both identities (StyleGAN3 set 48%; the public StyleGAN family reportedly below the verification threshold) are verdicts about generator detection.

The plan does not state the threat model for identity claims. An attacker who restores the code length (or pushes the morph away from the average face) keeps both matches and removes typicality completely. Any identity-typicality result holds for naive morphs only and must say so.

Generator twin sets at scale (D3 and D4, about 150 GPU-hours) can at best buy a per-generator averageness reader with the ceiling above. I agree with IDEAS_v1 on this; the lens gives the size of the ceiling.

The author's position recorded at about 16:00 (a one-photo reconstruction is generated-image detection, a different task; do not penalise morph detectors on it) conflicts with the ladder as preregistered, where AG1 prints 'R2 = a processed genuine image' and AD1's 'reads the benchmark' verdict for ViT-L/14 depends on the R1 to R2 step (share 0.70) more than on the history step (0.40). This must be settled before generator verdicts are read.
identity.first_experiment_tonight: GEO-0: does a real morph sit where identity geometry says it should? CPU only, about 30 minutes, no new image and no new feature extraction; one prereg page first. Inputs (glintr100 embeddings that exist now): /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/fr_emb_built.npz (built R3, R4, NC for 534 hosts and two tools, plus FRLL), /mnt/t7/smad_next/AR1/pool_src_emb.npz and frll_src_emb.npz (source photos H, S, R), /home/narolski/smad-next/experiments/AR1/pool.csv (pairs), /mnt/t7/smad_heldout/a46/feat/a46_feat.npz (FRLL gallery, a43_B and a43_D, reconstructions, published MorDIFF and DiM morphs, native and E7 controls). Four reads, fixed before looking: (1) Fidelity F = cos(embedding of the built image, normalised sum of its two source embeddings), for twins and for morphs. At least 0.90 means the midpoint model holds; 0.75 or less means the off-span part dominates, and then the question is whether that part is larger for morphs than for twins. (2) Mean-direction gain of R4 and R3 relative to the host photo against the predictions 1.27 and 1.03. (3) A head fitted only on virtual morphs and virtual twins of FRGC and colorFERET source embeddings (5 folds by person), applied unchanged to real AR1 R4 vs R3 and R4 vs host photo, to a43_B vs a43_D and to published diffusion morphs vs reconstructions, with controls native vs E7 and reconstruction vs aligner copy. Go for the identity component: at least 0.65 with lower bound above 0.60 on both landmark and DiffAE, controls inside 0.45 to 0.55. Kill: 0.55 or less on both. (4) Lambda and the ceiling per cosine bin, printed beside AD1's R2 vs R4 values. Free riders in the same hour, from existing score files: the shrink-law correlation for the released detectors on published morphs (idea 2) and the potent-subset re-read of AD1 and AG5 (idea 7). The result decides three things at once: whether FR-space identity typicality exists for real morphs and with which sign, how large the honest ceiling is for generator cells, and whether an FR-space arm belongs in T4. Next morning, if GEO-0 passes or shows a larger span deficit for morphs: the 20-GPU-minute amplitude and span-deficit probe of idea 4 and the oracle-distillation heads of idea 3 on the shared feature cache.
identity.detectability_analysis:
Disclosure: I formed my list before I found ideas/IDEAS_v1.md and ideas/SEEDS_main.md in the folder; I read them afterwards and mark overlaps. Their general account (superposition, photo averaging, identity averaging; the data-processing argument for generators; the attacker can restore length) matches mine. What this lens adds or corrects follows.

1. Geometry on the unit sphere. FR embeddings are compared after length normalisation, and FR training spreads identities over the sphere. So the thin-shell argument (a morph sits at 0.71 of the usual distance from the mean, separation grows with the square root of the number of identity dimensions) holds in a generator's code space or in a shape model, but not in FR space, where length is discarded and, before normalisation, measures image quality. In FR direction space a linear morph is (xA + xB)/sqrt(2(1+c)), c being the cosine of the two source embeddings. To first order its distribution equals that of a single photo, except that the component along the population mean is multiplied by kappa(c) = sqrt(2/(1+c)); at mixing fraction a it is 1/sqrt(1 - 2a(1-a)(1-c)). Best possible AUC of any reader of the embedding: Phi((kappa_morph - kappa_negative) x Lambda / sqrt 2), with Lambda = sqrt(mu' Sigma^-1 mu), the Mahalanobis length of the population mean. Lambda is not in the record. From the FMR 0.1% threshold 0.283 on FRGC and colorFERET (AR1 gate G-b) and an assumed mean impostor cosine of 0.03 to 0.08, I estimate 2 to 4.5.

Ceiling table, morph against one photo, AUC for Lambda 2 / 3 / 4: random pair (c = 0.03, kappa 1.39) 0.71 / 0.80 / 0.87; AR1 median pair (c = 0.23, kappa 1.27) 0.65 / 0.72 / 0.78; strong look-alike (c = 0.5, kappa 1.15) 0.59 / 0.63 / 0.67. Morph against same-person morph (twin cosine 0.87, kappa 1.03) at c = 0.23: 0.63 / 0.69 / 0.75. Identity typicality in FR space is real but tops out near 0.65 to 0.80 for benchmark-like pairs. It cannot carry a state-of-the-art claim, and a generator-cell R2 vs R4 result of 0.75 or more should be treated as suspicious.

2. Fidelity can erase even that. The formula assumes the morph's embedding is the normalised sum of its sources. The only in-house number (EXPERIMENTS.md S6: pseudo-morphs sit at cosine about 0.6 from both sources, which are 0.31 apart; the linear value is 0.81) implies a fidelity of about 0.74, so about 45% of the embedding's energy lies outside the span of the two sources. If that part is unstructured, the gain 1.27 becomes 0.94 and the typicality sign flips. If it is structured (the FR network's reaction to two superposed identities), it may be what the A46 d2 probe found (0.68 with clean controls). Fidelity for twins and for morphs is the first number to get.

3. What cannot work, and why. (a) Recovering the two contributors: see the first objection; theory and two in-house failures agree. (b) Part-wise identity agreement on uniform blends: the agreement of two region embeddings of a morph is (g + i)/sqrt((1+c_r)(1+c_s)), equal to the genuine level g to first order; only splice or mosaic morphs differ, by at most 50%. (c) FR feature norm and face-quality scores: quality measures, so history cues by design. (d) Neighbour density, hubness, number of gallery matches against a gallery that does not hold the contributors: all reduce to the same one-dimensional mean-direction statistic as typicality. (e) The gallery oracle (top-1 minus top-2 cosine, AUC 1.000) is not single-image detection; it needs the contributors enrolled.

4. Per family.
Landmark (pixel blend after warp). Detectable: superposition of two different persistent-feature maps, with strength L = 2a(1-a)(1-c) (0.07 for the AR1 twins, 0.38 for the AR1 morphs); exact averaging of landmark shape, including left-right asymmetry, which should stay near c = 0 even for look-alikes (an oracle check from the stored .tem files takes seconds; IDEAS_v1 M1 and M6 cover the scores); identity typicality up to the ceiling; inner against outer identity for splice tools. Not detectable: who the contributors are; a second identity when the pair is very similar. Fakeable by processing: loss of fine texture, feature norm.
GAN (code average or optimised code). Detectable: typicality only, and only for potent morphs. In the generator's own code space it is strong (code spread alone gave AUC 1.000 on the StyleGAN3 set, A39), but it measures averageness of everything (pose, background, light), and a one-person render moved toward the average is the same kind of image, so spread-matched renders are an equivalent image, not a control. Not detectable: a second identity as such; anything once the code length is restored.
Diffusion (DiffAE, MorDIFF, DiM: semantic code averaged, noise map interpolated on the sphere). One coherent render, so no superposition. Typicality up to the ceiling; the existing FR-space probe reads 0.59 to 0.68 against one-photo reconstructions while all three releases read 0.40 to 0.49 (AD1). Greedy-DiM and MIPGAN optimise towards both identities, so typicality is not guaranteed there.

5. What the ideas need from the open ruling. All seven treat a one-photo reconstruction as a non-morph and run under either ruling. But if a reconstruction counts as a processed genuine image, the best honest generator-family result is bounded by the table above, and no detector can be both state of the art and shortcut-free there. The author's position recorded at about 16:00 (reconstruction is generated-image detection, a different task) removes that bound: the generator contrast becomes history-matched camera photo (R1) against morph, and reading the render is acceptable. This lens supports that position. The typicality ideas also need two more statements: a one-person image moved toward the average face counts as manipulated, and the threat model is the naive attacker who does not restore length.

6. How this feeds one network. The identity parts are validators and bounds more than a detector: the shrink law (idea 2) and the ceiling (idea 1) go into the audit and the method tables; the oracle target (idea 3) is an auxiliary output of whichever single trunk is chosen; an FR trunk (idea 4) is an arm of T4. A CLIP trunk plus an FR trunk would be two networks and is not allowed; if CLIP stays, the FR teacher is used at training time only.
identity.sota_definition: From this lens. State of the art: on the ladder, one network (five seeds, last checkpoint) has the lowest error for potent morphs (both contributors verified at a false match rate of 1 in 1,000 with photos not used in the build) against processed genuine images, in every family, paired over persons against every released detector. Native benchmark numbers are printed beside it but are not the criterion. Shortcut-free needs three things a processing cue cannot produce: (1) silence between genuine constructions (R0 vs R1, and R0 vs R2 for landmark tools, folded AUC at most 0.60); (2) inside the morph class of one tool or generator, where history is constant, the score rises with contributor dissimilarity 1 - cos(A, B) and with mixing fraction (rank correlation with lower bound above 0); (3) on generator cells, R2 vs R4 does not exceed the identity ceiling measured for that pair-similarity range; a detector above the ceiling is reading something other than identity and must be audited further. For generator families the honest claim is 'reaches X of the ceiling' plus, if the author confirms the 16:00 position, error against history-matched camera photos (R1); it is not a superiority claim on two-identity reading.
